Walter Hale walks out with his son David to read what neither of them can make out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0003"><em>The boundary stones set</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0004"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The hungry year at Doire ghlas* (Doire ghlas). The stores that came over the water from an Tìr Thall come no more, and in their first year alone the northern settlements go short of grain. Tuathaich memory puts the dead at Doire ghlas above two hundred. The Dia-thìrich made no count.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVI-1002"><em>The north's first harvest falls short</em>, 31 an Cèitean, SE 1</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EVI-1003"><em>The Caol mhòr catch shared by households</em>, 2 an t-Ògmhios, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1009"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The guard posted at the heads of the north roads* (Caol mhòr). The council sets a guard-post on every road running north out of the settled country, a captain and a dozen men at each, to hold the line the columns had walked in winter and to turn back any who wander south of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0001"><em>The Tuathaich homeland fixed</em>, 22 am Màrt, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1010"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *Ailean mac Iain rides as tally-clerk to the guard*. A young clerk of the council's service is sent to ride between the new guard-posts with a book, counting who passes north, who turns back, and who is too sick to walk, so that the council should have some record of the settling beyond the guard's own word.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0001"><em>The Tuathaich homeland fixed</em>, 22 am Màrt, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1011"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The last column counted through at the Caol mhòr road*. Forty-one souls are counted through the guard-post on the Caol mhòr road, the last column of the winter's walking, two dying before evening; after them the road stands empty, and the tally-clerk's book records no further column that year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0001"><em>The Tuathaich homeland fixed</em>, 22 am Màrt, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1012"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The council's word on the homeland read at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). The council's law fixing the Tuathaich homeland in the north is read from the steps of the harbour-house at Caol mhòr before a wet crowd, first in Dia-thìris, then, by the council's own order, in the humans' tongue for those who have no other.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0001"><em>The Tuathaich homeland fixed</em>, 22 am Màrt, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1013"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *Walter Hale found to read the council's word into the humans' tongue* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale, once a harbour clerk of Ros bheag, is fetched from the crowd at Caol mhòr to render the council's proclamation into the humans' tongue, and reads it plainly, without the first reader's polish, to a crowd that takes it in near silence.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0001"><em>The Tuathaich homeland fixed</em>, 22 am Màrt, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1014"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *Hale's correction entered in a clerk's margin* (Caol mhòr). Asked how his rendering of the council's word differed from the paper he was given, Hale tells Ailean mac Iain that the truer word for what was done to the north was not "settled" but "held"; Ailean writes the two words in the margin of his own copy, unasked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0001"><em>The Tuathaich homeland fixed</em>, 22 am Màrt, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1015"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The humans' chapel at Ros bheag shut for good* (Ros bheag). Word reaches Caol mhòr that the humans' chapel at Ros bheag, shut since the crossing closed, is to be shut for good on the council's order; Walter Hale, once the town's harbour clerk, brings the news to Ailean mac Iain without asking anything of him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1016"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The Ros bheag bell carted north* (Ros bheag). The council's men take down the bell of the shut chapel at Ros bheag and cart it away roped in sacking, bound, it is said, for wherever in the north the humans' faith may still be kept; Ailean mac Iain sees the cart pass and notes it without comment.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1017"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *Meal carried from Caol mhòr to Doire ghlas* (Caol mhòr). The householders of Caol mhòr send three cartloads of oats and salt fish ten miles inland to Doire ghlas in the depth of the hungry winter, and Walter Hale walks with them, carrying the town's meal and, unlooked for, its grief.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1018"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The graves on the rise above Doire ghlas* (Doire ghlas). Above ten dead of the hungry winter, children among them, are buried in shallow graves on the rise above Doire ghlas, dug close together in half-frozen ground; the earliest of the winter's dead had already been buried singly, unrecorded, before the town thought to keep any count.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1019"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *Walter Hale's day-book begun* (Caol mhòr). Home from Doire ghlas, Walter Hale buys a fishmonger's ledger and writes the town's name and a number in it by lamplight, the first line of a private accounting of the hungry year's dead that no council south of the guard-stone has asked for or knows exists.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1020"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *Seed oats taken from the Doire mhin mill on credit* (Doire mhin). With the hungry winter not yet spent, the Tuathaich shires take seed oats from the mill at Doire mhin on credit against the coming harvest, the first debt of its kind the north carries into the new kingdom's account books.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1021"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The names pinned in the Doire ghlas church porch* (Doire ghlas). In the first mild week of spring a woman of the parish goes house to house through Doire ghlas gathering the names of the hungry year's dead, and pins them, above fifteen strips of paper in a dozen hands, along the boards of the church porch, where the town comes to call it the porch of the names.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1022"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *Walter Hale reads the porch of the names* (Doire ghlas). Walter Hale walks the ten miles to Doire ghlas a second time to read the names pinned in the church porch, and copies every one into a second book begun that winter, keeping the town's own count beside his, though neither squares exactly with the other.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1023"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1** — *The herring return to the Caol mhòr grounds* (Caol mhòr). By the second spring the herring come back to the Caol mhòr grounds in numbers not seen since before the Severance, and the town, having taken nothing from the sea that winter that it did not share, takes the shoals as the sea's answer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0005"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2** — *The human counting-houses emptied* (Ros dhomhain). Clerks of the council enter the human administration's counting-houses at Cathair dhearg, Ros dhomhain and Seann Skell and carry off every written thing. What the raids of the war have left of the tithe ledgers is boxed with the rest, unread, for few of the clerks can read the humans' hand.
- <a id="ev-EVI-1024"></a>**20 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2** — *Ailean set to the counting-house at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Ailean mac Iain is set to the humans' counting-house at Cathair dhearg to box the north wall's tithe rolls unread, and says nothing of the letters a Mission reader taught him as a boy, for a clerk who reads aloud what he is told only to box is not a clerk kept long.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0005"><em>The human counting-houses emptied</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1025"></a>**21 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2** — *The fire-damaged tithe rolls boxed as loose leaves* (Cathair dhearg). Where the counting-house fire at Cathair dhearg burned a shelf's ledgers through the middle rather than whole, Ailean gathers the crumbling leaves as best their order can be guessed and marks the crate that the order is his own guess and not to be trusted past that.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0005"><em>The human counting-houses emptied</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1026"></a>**23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2** — *The Ros dhomhain tariff copied into Dia-thìris* (Ros dhomhain). At the harbour offices of Ros dhomhain, Ailean copies the humans' tariff tables clause by clause into Dia-thìris, building the words for duties his own tongue had never before had cause to name, and the duty itself stands unchanged under its new ink.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0005"><em>The human counting-houses emptied</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1027"></a>**30 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2** — *The district surveys found behind a locked grating* (Seann Skell). In the whole counting-house at Seann Skell in the west, Ailean forces a locked grating and finds eleven rolled district surveys, the only whole survey of the island's fields anywhere to be had, each walked, measured and scaled by the humans' own hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0005"><em>The human counting-houses emptied</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1028"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, SE 2** — *The surveys boxed apart and labelled for the council* (Seann Skell). Ruairidh orders the district surveys boxed apart from the tithe rolls, for the council's own clerks rather than the reckoners, and Ailean chalks the crate's lid with six words rather than a description: the shires will be drawn on them.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0005"><em>The human counting-houses emptied</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1029"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, SE 2** — *The state's seal begun at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). In the same week as the proclamation, the council's engraver at Cathair dhearg begins cutting a seal for the state's own letters, to be set upon documents no different in kind from the ones Ailean spent the summer boxing unread.
- <a id="ev-V-0006"></a>**10 an t-Iuchar, SE 2** — *The north-west ports without a master* (Inis àrsaidh). At Ceann mhòr, Cathair gheal and Inis àrsaidh the humans' harbour officers had sailed with the last ships before the crossing closed, and taken their keys with them. The Tuathaich fishermen break the locks of the harbour stores and share out what they find, house by house.
- <a id="ev-EVI-1030"></a>**12 an t-Iuchar, SE 2** — *The harbour store's lock broken at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). A fisherman of Ceann mhòr breaks the lock of the humans' harbour store with a hammer and stands back to let the town see what is inside, and it is the town, not the man who struck the lock, that shares the rope, canvas and salt out house by house within the hour.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0006"><em>The north-west ports without a master</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1031"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, SE 2** — *The unfished nets loosed at Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). A whole loft of nets that had never been fished goes out to every boat in the harbour at Cathair gheal on a single tide, and the fleet fishes that year with gear it never paid a coin for and never afterward wonders whose it had been.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0006"><em>The north-west ports without a master</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1032"></a>**22 an t-Iuchar, SE 2** — *The reckoning drawn up by three women of Inis àrsaidh* (Inis àrsaidh). At Inis àrsaidh, poorer and smaller than its neighbours, three women of the town draw up on the spot the reckoning of who has a boat and who has none, and so who needs rope or salt the more, with no office to do it and none afterward to say they did it wrong.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0006"><em>The north-west ports without a master</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1033"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, SE 2** — *The north-west locks left unanswered* (Ceann mhòr). No maor comes north to ask who struck the first lock at Ceann mhòr, Cathair gheal or Inis àrsaidh before the following spring, by which time there is nothing left locked to account for, and the towns' own telling of the broken stores hardens into the kind of story a place keeps because it likes its shape.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0006"><em>The north-west ports without a master</em>, 10 an t-Iuchar, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0007"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, SE 2** — *Rìoghachd Dia-thìr declared* (Cathair dhearg). The state names itself a kingdom, though it is ruled as before. Its own records carry the same contradiction to this day.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EVI-1029"><em>The state's seal begun at Cathair dhearg</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1034"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, SE 2** — *Rìoghachd Dia-thìr proclaimed from the counting-house steps* (Cathair dhearg). A herald reads the council's proclamation from the steps of the Cathair dhearg counting-house, naming the state Rìoghachd Dia-thìr and the years of settling complete; Ailean stands in the crowd and does not cheer, thinking the naming a kind of label, true as far as it goes and silent about the rest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0007"><em>Rìoghachd Dia-thìr declared</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1035"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, SE 2** — *The proclamation read at the market crosses of the south* (Cathair dhearg). Copies of the proclamation styling the state Rìoghachd Dia-thìr are read at the market crosses of every southern town within the fortnight, in the same flat, official voice, whatever crowd happens to be standing near enough to hear it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0007"><em>Rìoghachd Dia-thìr declared</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0008"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, SE 2** — *The Moot at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). Tuathaich householders of the northern towns meet at Caol mhòr and choose for their speaker Walter Hale, once a harbour clerk. The Moot has no standing in Dia-thìrich law. It meets all the same and keeps its own minutes, which run unbroken from that day to this.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-1013"><em>Walter Hale found to read the council's word into the humans' tongue</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0009"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, SE 2** — *The council of the kingdom seated* (Cathair dhearg). A royal council of twelve is seated at Cathair dhearg, drawn from the custodian families and the captains of the Severance war. Its minute-books are the oldest unbroken record of the state in this age.
- <a id="ev-EVI-1500"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, SE 2** — *The Moot votes its first winter measures* (Caol mhòr). The households gathered at Caol mhòr vote, in the same sitting that opens the Moot's book, to lay by grain against the coming winter and to keep watch on the north roads, having buried too many of their own the winter before to trust the season a second time unwarned.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0008"><em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1501"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, SE 2** — *The Doire ghlas dead voted into the Moot's record* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale tells the gathered households what he counted on the rise above Doire ghlas and what the church porch's names afterward told him, and the Moot votes, without a voice raised against it, that the count stand as the north's own record of that winter's dead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0004"><em>The hungry year at Doire ghlas</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 1</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-V-0008"><em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1502"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, SE 2** — *The granary founded at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). The Moot sets a common store under lock in the harbour-house cellar, each household to give what it can spare, and names three keepers answerable for it: a harbour man trusted with a scale, a smith of Doire ghlas, and a widow of the hungry year who had buried two children in it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0008"><em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1503"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, SE 2** — *The Moot's letter drafted for the council* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale drafts, and the Moot amends and approves, four careful lines telling the council at Cathair dhearg of the households met at Caol mhòr and of a winter's dead the north had buried and counted without the south's knowledge, asking nothing beyond that the fact be noted.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0008"><em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1504"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, SE 2** — *Robert Carrick carries the Moot's letter south* (Caol mhòr). Peg Carrick's younger brother Robert, fifteen and never before further from Caol mhòr than Doire ghlas, a carter, carries the letter south to Cathair dhearg with it sewn into the lining of his coat, and is the better part of a fortnight on a road he does not know.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0008"><em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1505"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, SE 2** — *The Moot's letter received and filed* (Cathair dhearg). A clerk at the harbour-house in Cathair dhearg takes the Moot's letter from Robert Carrick's hand, tells him it will be seen to, and sends him home with no answer; the disposal, once the letter reaches the council chamber, is three words in the state's own minute-book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0009"><em>The council of the kingdom seated</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1506"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, SE 2** — *Ailean mac Iain and Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill sworn under-clerks* (Cathair dhearg). On the twenty-third of an t-Sultain the council's newest under-clerks are sworn on the custodians' worn oath-book, Ailean mac Iain among them and, beside him, Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill, a council clerk's daughter of the capital who has wanted the office since she was old enough to know what a minute-book was for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0009"><em>The council of the kingdom seated</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1507"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, SE 2** — *The council of twelve seated and its chairs filled* (Cathair dhearg). Twelve chairs are filled at Cathair dhearg, drawn from the custodian families and the captains of the Severance war: among them Fearchar mac Raghnaill, whose company's roll was kept the summer before; Beathag nic Artair of the old custodian houses; Griogair mac Tormoid of the western shore; and Cailean mac Sheumais, who commanded a company at the fords of the western hills.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0009"><em>The council of the kingdom seated</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1508"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, SE 2** — *A councillor asks what a Moot is* (Cathair dhearg). When the Moot's letter is read before the twelve, Cailean mac Sheumais asks plainly what a Moot is; no one in the chamber can answer with any certainty beyond Fearchar mac Raghnaill's memory of the word from a harbour clerk at Caol mhòr, and the letter is moved to be filed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0009"><em>The council of the kingdom seated</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1509"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, SE 2** — *The gathering of northern households takes the name Moot* (Caol mhòr). In the weeks after its first sitting the gathering of the north's households comes, without a vote taken on it, to be called the Moot, a word one of its own pursers remembered from an old book of the humans' law, half in earnest and half against themselves.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0008"><em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1510"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 2** — *Ailean sent to the Ros dhomhain sheds* (Ros dhomhain). A month after his swearing, Ailean mac Iain is sent from Cathair dhearg to Ros dhomhain to help Dùghall mac Iain turn the humans' tariff into Dia-thìris, line by line, since the harbour cannot wait for a tariff written fresh.
- <a id="ev-EVI-1511"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 2** — *Dùghall mac Iain's reason for copying, not writing anew* (Ros dhomhain). Dùghall mac Iain tells Ailean he keeps the humans' sums and changes only the words, since a skipper who has long paid a known tariff pays it gladly to a new hand, and a tariff written fresh would only be cheated the more freely for its newness.
- <a id="ev-EVI-1512"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, SE 2** — *Ailean's private book begun* (Ros dhomhain). At Ros dhomhain, Ailean begins a private book of his own, bound in undyed leather, in which he sets beside his day's plain clerking the things said to him that seem worth keeping, though he does not yet know their use.
- <a id="ev-V-0010"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, SE 3** — *The harbour-houses of Ros dhomhain taken over* (Ros dhomhain). The customs sheds that the humans built at Ros dhomhain, the greatest port of the kingdom, pass to Dia-thìrich harbour-masters. The first of them, Dùghall mac Iain, keeps the humans' tariff for want of another, and in the years after puts it into Dia-thìris line by line.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-1510"><em>Ailean sent to the Ros dhomhain sheds</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 2</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-1511"><em>Dùghall mac Iain's reason for copying, not writing anew</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 2</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EVI-1512"><em>Ailean's private book begun</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, SE 2</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0011"></a>**11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 3** — *The ship sent north* (Muir Mhanannain). The council sends a ship out past the north-western capes and north-about to seek the crossing the humans used. She returns after a month of grey water with nothing to tell: no land, no ship, no sign of the passage. No second ship is sent. The priests of Manannan at Seann Skell say that the lord of the sea has shut the eastern sea again, as they have prayed him to since the Crossing.
- <a id="ev-V-0012"></a>**19 an t-Ògmhios, SE 3** — *Niall crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Niall, first ruler of the restored kingdom, takes the throne at Cathair dhearg by Macha's rite. His is the first name in the line that the state's chronicles keep unbroken from this year on.
- <a id="ev-V-0013"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *A saying enters speech* (Cathair dhearg). The crowning passes with so little dispute that 'mar a thàinig Niall', the way Niall came, becomes a saying for any smooth handing-on of power. It is first found written in a tavern ledger at Cathair dhearg, against a debt settled without argument.
- <a id="ev-V-0014"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *The shires drawn* (Cathair dhearg). The council divides the kingdom into siorrachdan, each named for its seat, and keeps most of the human administration's district lines under the new names. The humans' surveys are the only whole ones on the island; the kingdom uses them and says nothing of it.
- <a id="ev-V-0014a"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *The windy coast left out* (Seann Vell). The shire lines stop where the humans' survey stopped, at the edge of the great moss of the far north-west. The windy coast beyond, an Oirthir Ghaothach, with its sealers and fowlers, is set in no shire and given no maor. The council's minute says only that it 'is not in the survey'.
- <a id="ev-V-0014b"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *The island shires* (Eilean dhìreach). Two rocks that each kept a customs station of the Administration, Eilean dhìreach off the Tuathaich coast and Eilean ìseal off the east coast, are kept as shires of their own, for the council has no rule for folding one district into its neighbour. Neither has a town to name it, and each shire takes the name of its island.
- <a id="ev-V-0014c"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *The market of Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). At the drawing of the shires the Tuathaich of Ceann mhòr are granted a market right for the north-west coast. Its court sits in the harbour store whose locks the fishermen broke. Fish, whale-oil, seal-oil, amber, dyes and the tobacco of the concession farms are sold there.
- <a id="ev-EVI-1513"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *Ailean named tally-clerk for An Sireadh* (Cuan shean). The council names Ailean mac Iain tally-clerk for the ship sent north-about to seek the crossing, and he rides hard for Cuan shean to be aboard by the sailing day, leaving the Ros dhomhain tariff a third finished.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0011"><em>The ship sent north</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1514"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *An Sireadh's log kept and filed* (Cuan shean). Ailean keeps An Sireadh's log the length of her voyage, heading, wind and soundings set down plainly through a month of grey water and mist, and the finished log is filed with the council on her return.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0011"><em>The ship sent north</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1515"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *Aonghas mac Mhurchaidh turns the ship for home*. Sixteen days out with the stores a third gone, Aonghas mac Mhurchaidh orders An Sireadh about, telling Ailean the sea has not been found empty so much as it has refused, this once, to show itself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0011"><em>The ship sent north</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1516"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *The prayer said over An Sireadh's return* (Seann Skell). The priests of Manannan come down to the quay at Seann Skell in the west as An Sireadh makes her berth and say again the old prayer that the sea be kept shut, said first at her going and now at her coming home empty-handed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0011"><em>The ship sent north</em>, 11 an t-Ògmhios, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1517"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *Ailean learns of the crowning at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). Home after a month at sea, Ailean learns of Niall's crowning from an innkeeper near the harbour at Seann Skell in the west, and writes the day into his private book with nothing beside it, having seen nothing of it with his own eyes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0013"><em>A saying enters speech</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0012"><em>Niall crowned</em>, 19 an t-Ògmhios, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1518"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *The shire map drawn from the humans' survey* (Cathair dhearg). Through an Dùbhlachd, Ailean copies the humans' district survey onto a fresh sheet and sets the Dia-thìris names of the shires against it, for the council to show the twelve without embarrassment at governing by a stranger's paperwork.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0014"><em>The shires drawn</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1519"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *The minute that the windy coast is not in the survey* (Seann Vell). Where the humans' survey ends unmarked at the great moss, Ailean writes a single short line rather than leave the gap unexplained: that the windy coast is not in the survey, a line the council's copying afterward carries to every maor's court unremarked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0014a"><em>The windy coast left out</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1520"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *The two island shires entered on the map* (Eilean dhìreach). Finding no council rule for folding a small holding into its neighbour, Ailean enters the two customs-station rocks as shires of their own, each taking the name of the island it sits on and noted as holding no town.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0014b"><em>The island shires</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1521"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3** — *Ceann mhòr's market right entered on the map* (Ceann mhòr). The council grants the Ceann mhòr fishermen a market right for their two years' rough trading in the broken-locked harbour store, and Ailean sets the grant down as the smallest clause on the whole map, the one thing on it the townsfolk had already made true for themselves.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0014c"><em>The market of Ceann mhòr</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, SE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0015"></a>**4 am Faoilleach, SE 4** — *The maoir appointed* (Ceann mhòr). A maor is set over each shire to gather the Crown's dues and keep its peace. In the Tuathaich shires the maoir are Dia-thìrich, lodged in the seat towns. At Ceann mhòr the maor lives in the old human magistrate's house, and the townsfolk call it by its old name.
- <a id="ev-V-0015a"></a>**21 am Faoilleach, SE 4** — *The Crown's dues set* (Cathair dhearg). The council sets the dues the maoir shall gather: a head-due, cìs-cinn, on every household by the number of its heads, and a market-due, cìs-margaidh, on every sale made by a seller of the kingdom. The humans' harbour tariff at Ros dhomhain stands until the kingdom has a coin of its own to take the market-due in.
- <a id="ev-V-0015b"></a>**2 an Gearran, SE 4** — *The roll of arms* (Cathair dhearg). The council's clerks make Clàr nan Suaicheantas, a roll of arms, so that each maor may seal the letters of his court. The kingdom's arms are cut anew from the old seal of the custody, and every shire is given arms of its own. Many charges are copied from a book of arms left at the Residency, and so lions, parrots and crocodiles stand on the seals of shires where none was ever seen. The Dia-thìrich shires bear the pointed shield of the custody's seal; the Tuathaich shires keep the rounded shield of the humans' district seals. At Seann Skell in the west the house of Òrd Mhanannain asks for its badge, the yellow scorpion of Manannan's cup, and that shire alone of all the roll bears a scorpion.
- <a id="ev-V-0016"></a>**8 am Màrt, SE 4** — *The maor of Baile Mòr mhòr* (Baile Mòr mhòr). Coinneach mac Ailein, first maor of Siorrachd Baile Mòr mhòr, holds his court under the market roof of the town, for the humans' courthouse has burned. He keeps it there after the new courthouse is built, and so do those who follow him.
- <a id="ev-V-0017"></a>**3 an t-Ògmhios, SE 4** — *Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol*. The Great Wave falls without warning on the southern coast and lays waste Cnoc chaol, Cuan dhearg and Achadh mhin in a single night. It is the first disaster the new state meets by its own means.
- <a id="ev-V-0018"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, SE 4** — *The dead of the Great Wave counted* (Cuan dhearg). Relief parties from Cathair dhearg come to Cuan dhearg on the southern coast and count the dead of the three settlements at a little over forty. The harbour of Cuan dhearg is gone, and its boats are found in the fields behind the town. The wave has run on up the gulf as far as Ros gharbh, the seat of its shire, broken its quays and cast the gulf's fishing fleet on the headland. The town stands high and loses few of its people, but nearly every boat.
- <a id="ev-V-0019"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *Achadh mhin under salt* (Achadh mhin). The fields of Achadh mhin lie under salt and will not bear. The council moves the survivors to higher ground and pays for their seed from the treasury. It is the first relief the restored kingdom grants.
- <a id="ev-V-0020"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *Cnoc chaol rebuilt on the hill* (Cnoc chaol). Cnoc chaol is built again on the slope behind the old town, beyond the wave's reach. The old site is left as the water left it. The townsfolk call it an Tràigh Bhàthte, the drowned strand, and do not build there.
- <a id="ev-EVI-1522"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *The first maor's seal cut from the roll of arms*. The council's clerk Tòmas cuts the first working seal from Clàr nan Suaicheantas, the newly drawn roll of arms, for a maor of the south-west to press upon his letters; the shire's borrowed lion goes out sealing writs before the ink of the roll itself is fully dry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0015b"><em>The roll of arms</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1523"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *Coinneach mac Ailein settles the fishwives' stall-place* (Baile Mòr mhòr). In his first sitting under the market roof at Baile Mòr mhòr, the new maor Coinneach mac Ailein settles a two-year quarrel over a stall-place by asking the gathered stallholders for the truth of it rather than ruling from the bench alone, and takes their answer as his judgment.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0016"><em>The maor of Baile Mòr mhòr</em>, 8 am Màrt, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1524"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *The council votes a relief party for the southern coast* (Cathair dhearg). Before its morning sitting breaks, the council of twelve votes grain, blankets, timber and men down the coast road to Cuan dhearg, and orders a tally kept of what is found, the first time the twelve have met before full light since the Severance itself.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0017"><em>Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol</em>, 3 an t-Ògmhios, SE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0018"><em>The dead of the Great Wave counted</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1525"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *Ailean's tally-book of the wave begun* (Cuan dhearg). Ailean mac Iain, sent south with the relief party, opens a plain tally-book at Cuan dhearg and enters the first of what will be a summer's counting: boats found standing in the fields, wells fouled or sweet, dead named where they can be and marked only by place where they cannot.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0018"><em>The dead of the Great Wave counted</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1526"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *The dead of Cuan dhearg buried on the rise* (Cuan dhearg). Through the first fortnight after the wave, the dead of Cuan dhearg are carried up onto the rise above the old harbour line and buried in ground the sea has not reached, while the town's clerks mark by place what names cannot be recovered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0018"><em>The dead of the Great Wave counted</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1527"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *The boats left standing in the barley* (Cuan dhearg). The wrecked fishing boats of Cuan dhearg, carried inland by the wave and left standing among the barley behind the town, are judged too many to right before winter and are left through the harvest, one still upright in its furrow with its mast stepped.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0018"><em>The dead of the Great Wave counted</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1528"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *The treasury's first relief roll voted* (Cathair dhearg). On the count of a little over forty dead, the council votes seed and removal for the survivors of Achadh mhin out of the treasury without a due asked in return, over one councillor's question of cost, answered that a kingdom that finds silver for a roll of arms can find grain for its own dead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0019"><em>Achadh mhin under salt</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1529"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *Ros gharbh's fleet counted on the headland* (Ros gharbh). Ailean mac Iain walks the headland above Ros gharbh's harbour and counts the town's fishing fleet where the wave cast it, hull by hull, sound or stove, and carries the count south as proof that a town spared its people can still be ruined in its trade.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0018"><em>The dead of the Great Wave counted</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-1530"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 4** — *A hill shire questions its new arms*. A custodian's widow keeping a south-western shire's books asks the council's clerk whether a shire that never bore a badge under the old custody must bear one now, and is answered that any shire's writs are read faster at Cathair dhearg with a seal, borrowed beast or none, than without one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0015b"><em>The roll of arms</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0021"></a>**4 am Faoilleach, SE 5** — *Tonn* (Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol). In the survivors' accounts gathered by the relief parties, 'tonn', wave, is used of anything sudden and overwhelming. Within a generation the sense is heard across the south: 'tha e san tonn', he is in the wave of it.
- <a id="ev-V-0022"></a>**1 an Giblean, SE 5** — *The wave's reach on Eilean mhin* (Eilean mhin). The Great Wave passes also over the low island of Eilean mhin off the southern coast, where none then lived the year round. The shepherds who summered there do not go back.
- <a id="ev-EVI-1531"></a>**24 an Giblean, SE 5** — *Ros gharbh's boats rebuilt* (Ros gharbh). Through the following year Ros gharbh borrows hulls from harbours the wave did not reach while shipwrights from beyond the gulf raise its fleet anew on the cleared beach, one keel at a time, until the last boat is launched and the town's people begin calling that whole year simply the bad year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0018"><em>The dead of the Great Wave counted</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, SE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0023"></a>**30 an Giblean, SE 5** — *The old human coinage withdrawn*. All the humans' coin still in hand is cried down and ceases to be money. Within a year a new coinage of the Rìoghachd takes its place, minted with ink of coal dust in its seal.
- <a id="ev-V-0024"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, SE 5** — *The mint at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). A mint is set up in the old human counting-house at Cathair dhearg under Fearchar mac Dhòmhnaill, called Fearchar Bonn. The seal of each coin is pressed with an ink ground from coal dust, so that a clipped coin shows the colour at its edge.
- <a id="ev-V-0025"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, SE 5** — *The northern savings voided* (Caol mhòr). The Tuathaich households kept what savings they had in the humans' coin. Now it is withdrawn, and their savings are worth their weight in metal and no more. The Moot at Caol mhòr petitions the council for an exchange. The petition is received and filed.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2000"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, SE 5** — *Walter Hale's tally of the cried-down savings* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale goes house to house at Caol mhòr with his day-book, counting what the town's households had kept back in the humans' coin now the council has cried it down. The sum comes to something over four hundred marks across better than two hundred households, none of it large, all of it now worth its weight as metal alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0025"><em>The northern savings voided</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, SE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2001"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, SE 5** — *Fearchar Bonn's four failed strikings* (Cathair dhearg). At the mint in the old counting-house at Cathair dhearg, Fearchar mac Dhòmhnaill spends a winter grinding coal dust fine enough to hold in a coin's seal without fouling the die, ruining four strikings of good silver before the ink and the binder are right. The fifth striking is shown to the treasury and kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0024"><em>The mint at Cathair dhearg</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, SE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2002"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, SE 5** — *Òrd Mhacha's blessing of the first striking* (Cathair dhearg). The first true coin of the Rìoghachd is blessed by Òrd Mhacha before it leaves the mint at Cathair dhearg, on the council's own instruction that the coal in its seal be reckoned a piece of the mountain carried out into every purse of the kingdom. The coin passes at the capital's markets within the month as though it had always been current.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0024"><em>The mint at Cathair dhearg</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, SE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2003"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, SE 5** — *A maor's clerk carries the new coin north* (Caol mhòr). In the autumn a young clerk of a southern maor's office rides to Caol mhòr with the first struck coin the Moot has seen, and, asked how a household of the south is managing the exchange, answers that he does not rightly know, his own family's savings having gone on the rent before the crying-down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0025"><em>The northern savings voided</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, SE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2004"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, SE 5** — *The Moot debates the wording of its petition* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr argues two evenings over a letter for the council, one voice wanting it to ask why the coin was cried down without warning north, another wanting no blame in it at all. Walter Hale's plain ask for a exchange mark for mark, without complaint, stands by the second evening nearly as he first wrote it.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0025"><em>The northern savings voided</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, SE 5</a>.</span>

## The Years SE 6 – 10

- <a id="ev-V-0026"></a>**2 an Gearran, SE 6** — *Joseph Marlow's ploughshares* (Doire mhin). At Doire mhin in the north the smith Joseph Marlow melts down his neighbours' withdrawn coin and casts it into ploughshares, and sells them back at the cost of the charcoal. The Tuathaich songs name him yet.
- <a id="ev-V-0027"></a>**3 am Màrt, SE 6** — *The coin at Inis thais* (Inis thais). At Inis thais on the south-west coast the new coin is scarce for most of the year, and the merchants trade in chits written on the paper of the house of the Stone. When the coin comes the chits are redeemed at the house's door, and the house keeps a tenth.
- <a id="ev-V-0028"></a>**18 an Giblean, SE 6** — *Òrd Bhrìde given its doctrine*. The Coal Rite, Òrd Bhrìde, the order that keeps Brìde's flame and Crom's stone, is given a settled doctrine within the Old Faith. Through the long ages it had kept its flame by custom and by no written creed; now its doctrine is built upon the leyline and the unbroken line of the coal-touched.
- <a id="ev-V-0029"></a>**17 an Cèitean, SE 6** — *The first high custodian of the Rite* (Seann Skell). Dòmhnall mac Thormoid is named Àrd-choimheadaiche of Òrd Bhrìde and seated at Seann Skell on the southern coast, where the order's greatest house stands. His first charge is to write an order of worship. There had never been one.
- <a id="ev-V-0030"></a>**23 an Cèitean, SE 6** — *The Hawk houses refuse* (Cnoc bheag). The houses of Òrd an t-Seabhaig about Cnoc bheag refuse the new order of worship, holding that the older form of the Old Faith needs no custodian above the local altar. They are not compelled. Here begins the long quarrel of the Hawk and the Rite.
- <a id="ev-V-0030a"></a>**29 an Cèitean, SE 6** — *The hawk-house at Muileann naomh takes the order* (Muileann naomh). The hawk-house at Muileann naomh, southernmost of the Hawk's houses and farthest from Cnoc bheag, takes the Rite's written order of worship and becomes a house of Òrd Bhrìde. Its bell, the first hung in any hawk-house, now rings at the Rite's measured burnings. No other house of the Hawk follows.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2005"></a>**27 an t-Ògmhios, SE 6** — *The petition copied fair and sent twice* (Caol mhòr). David Hale copies his father's letter to the council a second time, so that one fair copy travels south with the winter carter and a second waits for the spring roads, on the reasoning that two letters in two hands are harder for a clerk to mislay than one. Both reach the council's chests within the year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0025"><em>The northern savings voided</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, SE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2006"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, SE 6** — *Ailean mac Iain files the Moot's letter* (Cathair dhearg). The Moot's letter asking an exchange for the north's voided savings reaches the council's chests and is read by the under-clerk Ailean mac Iain, who notes its date and seal, finds no standing order to answer it, and sets it down among that quarter's petitions marked with two words, received; filed, as his post requires.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0025"><em>The northern savings voided</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, SE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2007"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, SE 6** — *Joseph Marlow's first ploughshare* (Doire mhin). At his forge by the millrace at Doire mhin, Joseph Marlow melts down his own household's cried-down coin before any neighbour's, casting it into the flat shape a ploughshare wants, still bearing along one edge the ghost of a king's profile the mould has not erased.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0026"><em>Joseph Marlow's ploughshares</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2008"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, SE 6** — *Marlow's charge fixed at the price of the charcoal* (Doire mhin). Joseph Marlow sets his price for turning a neighbour's dead coin into a ploughshare at the cost of his charcoal alone, reasoning that a man should not pay twice for coin the council has already taken from him once. Half of Doire mhin brings him its savings before the winter is out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0026"><em>Joseph Marlow's ploughshares</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2009"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, SE 6** — *Harry Marlow promised to a Cuan shean yard* (Doire mhin). Harry Marlow, Joseph Marlow's eldest son, nine years old, is promised to a shipwright's yard at Cuan shean when he turns thirteen, on the word of a Cuan shean man who watched him true a plough-beam by eye at his father's forge without a level.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0030a"><em>The hawk-house at Muileann naomh takes the order</em>, 29 an Cèitean, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2010"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, SE 6** — *Joseph Marlow's song first sung at Doire mhin* (Doire mhin). A plain tune naming Joseph Marlow and his forge is first heard going quietly round Doire mhin that winter, sung under the breath of the women waiting their turn with a sackful of savings, though the smith himself will not sing it in front of a stranger.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0026"><em>Joseph Marlow's ploughshares</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2011"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, SE 6** — *The house of the Stone's chits redeemed at its door* (Inis thais). At Inis thais, where the new coin arrives slower than almost anywhere in the kingdom, the merchants trade the winter through on chits written against the word of the house of Òrd na Cloiche. When coin at last comes south in quantity, the chits are carried to the house's own door and redeemed there, less a tenth the house keeps for the keeping of them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0027"><em>The coin at Inis thais</em>, 3 am Màrt, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2012"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, SE 6** — *Hale sets down the answer he means to give the Moot* (Caol mhòr). Weighing Fearchar Bonn's coin against Joseph Marlow's ploughshare on his own table, Walter Hale writes for the Moot that a people waiting on an answer that never comes would do better to build, while it waits, the thing it asked for, since the waiting will be long and the ground does not stop wanting to be ploughed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0025"><em>The northern savings voided</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, SE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0026"><em>Joseph Marlow's ploughshares</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2013"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, SE 6** — *The first furrow cut with a coin-iron share* (Doire mhin). At the end of am Màrt the first furrow of Doire mhin's spring ploughing is cut behind a borrowed ox with one of Joseph Marlow's shares, turning a clean black line the length of the field, the humans' silver made over into iron for a north the council's coin has not yet reached.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0026"><em>Joseph Marlow's ploughshares</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2014"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, SE 6** — *The written order first read at the southern Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). In the hall of the greatest house of the Rite, Dòmhnall mac Thormoid reads aloud, for the first time, the order of worship he has spent the year composing: the leyline, the unbroken line of the coal-touched, and the measure of what may be burned. Eleven custodians and a scattering of witnesses from neighbouring houses hear it out in silence.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0029"><em>The first high custodian of the Rite</em>, 17 an Cèitean, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2015"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, SE 6** — *The houses of the Stone promise good will and nothing more* (Baile Mòr fhionn). Within the month a letter reaches Seann Skell from the houses of the Stone in the south-west, wishing the new order well and offering no further part in it. Dòmhnall mac Thormoid copies it into the first page of a plain ledger he begins that day, meaning to keep every letter the Rite sends or receives from then on.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2016"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, SE 6** — *The Hawk houses' letter of refusal* (Cnoc bheag). A letter comes to Seann Skell from the hawk-houses about Cnoc bheag, sealed with the mark of a bird with wings spread flat: the old form of the Rite has never needed a custodian above the local altar and sees no cause to answer to one now. It calls the new writing handsome, and not needed, and wishes the southern house no ill in going its own way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0030"><em>The Hawk houses refuse</em>, 23 an Cèitean, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2017"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, SE 6** — *Muileann naomh's bell first rung at a measured burning* (Muileann naomh). The hawk-house at Muileann naomh, far south of Cnoc bheag, takes up the written order entire and hangs a bell cast new for the ordered worship, the first any house of the Rite has raised for that purpose rather than a wedding or a warning. It is rung that summer at the year's measured burning before a small crowd gathered in the lane.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-V-0030"><em>The Hawk houses refuse</em>, 23 an Cèitean, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2018"></a>**21 an t-Samhain, SE 6** — *Dòmhnall mac Thormoid's book of correspondence begun* (Seann Skell). Watching a house answer him with silence rather than argument, the new high custodian begins a plain ledger to hold every letter the Rite sends or receives, the first such record any keeper of the flame has thought to make, so that a question once answered need not be answered from nothing a second time.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0030a"><em>The hawk-house at Muileann naomh takes the order</em>, 29 an Cèitean, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2019"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, SE 6** — *Dòmhnall mac Thormoid rides north to Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Summoned to be presented at court as the Rite's first high custodian, Dòmhnall mac Thormoid rides to the capital to press, unsuccessfully, for a share in Òrd Mhacha's keeping of the coronation regalia. He pays for his own lodging, no arrangement having been made for him, and returns south with only the high priest's refusal to enter in his book.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2020"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 6** — *The unbroken line left open in doctrine* (Seann Skell). Writing the order's page on the coal-touched, Dòmhnall mac Thormoid finds an old defence and a later gloss disagree on whether the unbroken line means blood or office, and sets the doctrine down to hold both readings rather than close either, having found no ground in the record to choose between them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0028"><em>Òrd Bhrìde given its doctrine</em>, 18 an Giblean, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0031"></a>**2 an Gearran, SE 7** — *The houses of the Stone stand aside* (Baile Mòr fhionn). The houses of Òrd na Cloiche in the south-west, whose Clach, the Lia Fàil, is not Crom's stone, are bidden to send witnesses to the settling of the Rite at Seann Skell. They send none, and a letter wishing it well.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-2015"><em>The houses of the Stone promise good will and nothing more</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0032"></a>**10 an Gearran, SE 7** — *The Moot's schoolhouse petition* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale asks the council for leave to open schools in the north that teach in the humans' tongue. The council answers that the kingdom's schools teach in Dia-thìris and it has no others. The Moot's minute calls the answer 'clear, at least'.
- <a id="ev-V-0033"></a>**26 an Gearran, SE 7** — *The crown's order and the court* (Cathair dhearg). The house of Òrd Mhacha at Cathair dhearg, the order of the capital and the crown, is given the keeping of the coronation regalia, which it had kept before the humans came. The Rite's high custodian asks a share in the keeping and is refused.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-2019"><em>Dòmhnall mac Thormoid rides north to Cathair dhearg</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0034"></a>**29 an t-Ògmhios, SE 7** — *The first census after the Severance*. The state counts its own people for the first time since it took back the island. The roll notes, and says no more of it, how few the coal-touched are.
- <a id="ev-V-0034a"></a>**30 an t-Iuchar, SE 7** — *The census of the faiths* (Baile chrom). The first census of the restored kingdom enters every town under the faith its people keep, the Old Faith, the Old Spirits or the Church. It is the first such roll since Seumas Bàn's clerks counted the rites at Dùn ìseal. On the far north-western cape beyond Baile chrom, where there is no town, the clerks find scattered families with no house of any faith, and on Eilean ghorm and the smallest islets no one to ask. All these they enter as *gun chreideamh*, without a faith.
- <a id="ev-V-0035"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, SE 7** — *The count taken from the road* (Doire ghlas). Dia-thìrich census clerks count the Tuathaich towns of Siorrachd Doire ghlas from the road and enter few of the houses. That same year the Moot keeps its own tally. The two totals differ by nearly a fifth, and each side holds to its own.
- <a id="ev-V-0036"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, SE 7** — *The circuit justices* (Cathair dhomhain). Justices are appointed to ride circuit among the shires, and the first of them is Eilidh nic Leòid of Cathair dhomhain. Her circuit takes in eleven shires of the south-west and is most of a year in the riding.
- <a id="ev-V-0036a"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, SE 7** — *The head-due first collected* (Cathair dhearg). The maoir gather the head-due for the first time, on the households the census counted, at eighteen purses on every five thousand heads, and take it with the harbour dues.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2021"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, SE 7** — *Copies of the order sent to every house of the Rite* (Seann Skell). By the last month of winter Dòmhnall mac Thormoid's two clerks finish fair copies of the order, each checked line by line against his own text, and he sends them to every house of the Old Faith still standing, the Hawk-houses among them, along with the houses of the Stone, Òrd Mhacha, and a last copy carried back to Muileann naomh in thanks.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0029"><em>The first high custodian of the Rite</em>, 17 an Cèitean, SE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2022"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, SE 7** — *The census asks of faith and finds none to answer for some*. The state's first census, sent to ask what households hold to as well as how many they number, meets on the far north-western cape and its islets a good many who give no creed at all. Finding no word in Dia-thìris that fits a household with nothing to declare, the clerks write against their names gun chreideamh, without a creed, and ride on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0034"><em>The first census after the Severance</em>, 29 an t-Ògmhios, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2023"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, SE 7** — *The two counts of Doire ghlas go uncorrected* (Doire ghlas). The state's roll and the Moot's own tally of the northern shire, taken the same season by different hands, are found afterward to differ by close to a fifth. Neither is sent to the other side to be checked against it, and both are filed, each true by its own reckoning, in the chest that kept it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0035"><em>The count taken from the road</em>, 15 an Lùnastal, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2024"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, SE 7** — *Eilidh nic Leòid's letter of office reaches Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). A council rider, delayed three days by flooded roads, brings Eilidh nic Leòid the letter naming her first among the circuit justices: eleven shires of the south-west to be ridden once in every twelvemonth, and a written record of every judgment to be carried back each year to the council's clerks.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0036"><em>The circuit justices</em>, 23 an Lùnastal, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2025"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, SE 7** — *Eilidh's first assize, held at Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). Before setting out on her circuit Eilidh nic Leòid sits her first cases at home: a boundary measured with a knotted cord rather than taken on either party's word, a debt found on the strength of an unburned receipt, and a fishmonger's short weight proved against the council's own standard.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0036a"><em>The head-due first collected</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2026"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, SE 7** — *The quarrel over the well at Muileann bhàn* (Muileann bhàn). A widow who once charged a penny a season for water from a spring now run dry, and the mason set to warden the town's new waterworks, bring their dispute over one well to the circuit justice's bench in the mill-yard, the town having no courtroom of its own.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2027"></a>**19 an t-Samhain, SE 7** — *Eilidh's ruling on the Muileann bhàn well* (Muileann bhàn). The justice rules that the dead spring's old custom cannot be transferred to water drawn by a different road and paid for from a different purse, but that the well's ground remains the widow's by custom, and the town's word is given that it will never be built over or fenced from her without leave.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0036a"><em>The head-due first collected</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2028"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, SE 7** — *The head-due first gathered along the southern circuit*. Maors' clerks set up their tables at the crossroads of the south-west shires and take the head-due, eighteen purses on every five thousand heads, for the first time in living memory. Eilidh nic Leòid, riding past more than one such table, keeps her own note of what she sees, though none of it is brought to her bench.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0036a"><em>The head-due first collected</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2029"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, SE 7** — *Eilidh's circuit calls at Inis thais* (Inis thais). The harbour court at Inis thais, kept well enough already by its own magistrate, hands up only two causes to the visiting justice, both turning on the ownership of a fishing boat after its owner died leaving no heir the town could agree on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0036a"><em>The head-due first collected</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2030"></a>**4 an Dùbhlachd, SE 7** — *Eilidh's circuit calls at Doire shean* (Doire shean). Sitting two days in the temple porch for want of a courtroom, the justice settles a dispute among four households over the right to dry nets on a stretch of shingle by asking after the shore's own long custom rather than any written law, which none had ever thought to write so far down the coast.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0036a"><em>The head-due first collected</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0037"></a>**3 am Màrt, SE 8** — *Muileann bhàn's waterworks* (Muileann bhàn). Muileann bhàn on the southern plain builds the first public waterworks of the restored kingdom: a stone tank on the hill, fed by the mill-race, with lead pipes to four street wells. The Guild of Hewers sends its surveyors to learn the making of it.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-2026"><em>The quarrel over the well at Muileann bhàn</em>, 19 an Dàmhair, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0038"></a>**10 an t-Sultain, SE 8** — *The Leòid ruling* (Seann Bhral). Sitting at Seann Bhral, Eilidh nic Leòid rules that land held by Tuathaich under human title passes to the Crown, and that the right to work it stays with the holders and their heirs. The ruling is cited in nearly every land case of the age after.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2031"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, SE 8** — *The maor of Seann Bhral asks a ruling of his own cousin* (Seann Bhral). Artair mac Lachlainn, maor of the western shire, meets the circuit justice at the town gate and asks her plainly to find for the Crown's grant, the household holding it being kin of his own. She hears the cause as she hears any other, and he sits through it without speaking.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0038"><em>The Leòid ruling</em>, 10 an t-Sultain, SE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2032"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, SE 8** — *The Tanner suit heard at Seann Bhral in the west* (Seann Bhral). A Tuathaich family holding four fields under a Company surveyor's title cut before the Severance is set against a Dia-thìreach household holding the Crown's newer grant of the same ground, made in ignorance that the land was occupied at all. Half the shire's Tuathaich households come to Seann Bhral to hear it argued.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0038"><em>The Leòid ruling</em>, 10 an t-Sultain, SE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2033"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, SE 8** — *The Leòid ruling copied to every maor's court of the circuit*. Eilidh nic Leòid has her ruling fair-copied to every maor's court of her eleven shires, with a note that any like cause be decided on like reasoning until the council itself says otherwise, reasoning that a law read differently in every court that hears it is no law at all.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0038"><em>The Leòid ruling</em>, 10 an t-Sultain, SE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0039"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, SE 8** — *The coal line repaired* (Muileann chrom). The railway the humans built from the central mountains to the sea, broken in three places in the Severance war, is mended as far as Muileann chrom. A Rail Board is formed at Cathair dhearg to run it, with a clerk, two engineers and the humans' timetable.
- <a id="ev-V-0040"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, SE 8** — *The bridge at Cathair dhearg re-dedicated* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). The stone bridge over the Abhainn dhomhain below the capital, rebuilt in the humans' day, is hallowed anew with a name-stone in Dia-thìris. The humans' stone is left in its place and turned to face the river.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2500"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, SE 8** — *The Rail Board's timetable hung at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). The mended line's copied timetable, carried over from the humans' own working papers, is hung on a board at the Muileann chrom terminus where the rails now end. Passengers and carters read it as they find it, since no one troubles to explain why a six-year-old kingdom keeps a dead people's hours.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0039"><em>The coal line repaired</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, SE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2501"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 8** — *The talk at the net-mending* (Baile chrom). Under the eaves of the net-store church at Baile chrom, the winter's net-mending turns to talk of Hannah Crane's word that the Grey Night vigil will be kept in the open. Some call it needless risk to an old office; others say it is overdue. No one carries the talk beyond the town.
- <a id="ev-V-0041"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, SE 9** — *The necropolis at Cnoc dhìreach* (Tuam Cnoc dhìreach). The shire of Ceann mhin closes the old burial ground at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach to new graves, for the vines have broken so many stones that no room can be found. Families of the town still tend the old graves, and some say the place is not empty after dark.
- <a id="ev-V-0042"></a>**13 an Gearran, SE 9** — *Eaglais nan Tuathach persists*. The Tuathaich communities keep their Church alive in the north. Quietly they keep also the telling of the First Canoe, the voyage of Naomh Breandan to the Isle of the Blessed, which the Dia-thìrich priesthood calls superstition still.
- <a id="ev-V-0043"></a>**14 am Màrt, SE 9** — *The Grey Night kept openly* (Baile chrom). At Baile chrom in the far north-west the vigil-keeper Hannah Crane holds the vigil of Rùn-dìomhair na h-Oidhche Glaise in the open, for the first time since the Severance. The sect keeps one night of silence in the year under Sìne, the Peaceful Goose, its name for the wild goose of the Holy Spirit. The bishops of the Church call the vigil irregular. Outsiders are not told which night it is.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVI-2501"><em>The talk at the net-mending</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0044"></a>**30 am Màrt, SE 9** — *The churches of the north* (Cnoc ghorm). Most Tuathaich towns keep An Eaglais, the Church their forebears brought at the Crossing; the Dia-thìrich of the west coast beside them keep Manannan's order. A church is built at Cnoc ghorm, the greatest in the north.
- <a id="ev-V-0044a"></a>**12 an Giblean, SE 9** — *The cattle-market at Muileann fhionn* (Muileann fhionn). Muileann fhionn, the mill-town the humans built to guard the northern landing, is granted a market right for the north-western inland country. The Tuathaich drovers bring their cattle and sheep to it, and from it the droves go south to Ceann leathan and the farms of the south-east. It grows to be the greatest cattle-market on the island.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2502"></a>**12 an Cèitean, SE 9** — *The old priest's counsel* (Baile chrom). Walking back from a burial, the priest of Baile chrom tells Hannah Crane that the vigil's keeping is hers to judge, having held his own office forty years by staying out of what belongs to another. It is the only word of encouragement she has from anyone before the night.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0043"><em>The Grey Night kept openly</em>, 14 am Màrt, SE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2503"></a>**4 an t-Ògmhios, SE 9** — *The maor's man watches and writes nothing* (Baile chrom). A clerk's assistant of Cnoc ghorm, lodging at Baile chrom on an unrelated errand, climbs a rise above the headland and watches Hannah Crane's vigil through the night from a distance. He carries no instruction to report it and no form to record it on, and the shire's returns for the week say nothing.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-V-0043"><em>The Grey Night kept openly</em>, 14 am Màrt, SE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2504"></a>**11 an t-Iuchar, SE 9** — *The bishops' letter kept behind the altar-cloth* (Baile chrom). Three bishops of the Church write to Baile chrom calling the open keeping of the Grey Night irregular, and ask, without commanding, that the custom be given up. Hannah Crane reads the letter twice and puts it away in the box that already keeps the town's oldest relic, and answers nothing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0043"><em>The Grey Night kept openly</em>, 14 am Màrt, SE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2505"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, SE 9** — *The Ros bheag bell raised at Cnoc ghorm* (Cnoc ghorm). The bell of the old chapel at Ros bheag, carted north at the Severance and crated in a barn for want of a tower to take it, is hung at last in the new church at Cnoc ghorm and rung on a market morning. Its sound carries to the shore road, farther than the town had thought a single bell could reach.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0044"><em>The churches of the north</em>, 30 am Màrt, SE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2506"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, SE 9** — *The hurdles built on the Muileann fhionn green* (Muileann fhionn). The town's carpenters spend most of a month raising pens on the old common green at Muileann fhionn, working from a plan one of them had seen used at a southern fair, to hold the cattle and sheep the new market right will bring down from the hill farms.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0044a"><em>The cattle-market at Muileann fhionn</em>, 12 an Giblean, SE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2507"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, SE 9** — *The first drove south from Muileann fhionn* (Muileann fhionn). Hill farmers who had always walked their beasts the long way south now bring them to the new market at Muileann fhionn, and from there the droves go on by the old tracks toward Ceann leathan. Within a few seasons the green stands trodden to mud on every market morning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0044a"><em>The cattle-market at Muileann fhionn</em>, 12 an Giblean, SE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2508"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, SE 9** — *A young wife of Muileann fhionn keeps her own watch* (Baile chrom). A woman newly married into Baile chrom from Muileann fhionn, who asked Hannah Crane whether she was not afraid to keep the vigil alone, climbs the headland herself the night it is kept and watches from a careful distance. She tells no one, not even her husband, that she went.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-V-0043"><em>The Grey Night kept openly</em>, 14 am Màrt, SE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0045"></a>**29 an Giblean, SE 10** — *The church school at Cnoc ghorm* (Cnoc ghorm). The church at Cnoc ghorm opens a school for its priests. It teaches in the humans' tongue and reads the Bible in the Dia-thìris text its preachers use on the west coast. In all the north, both are taught there only.
- <a id="ev-V-0046"></a>**11 an Cèitean, SE 10** — *The border wall proposed*. A fixed boundary between the Dia-thìrich and the Tuathaich country is proposed for the first time. It is refused as needless, for the two peoples already keep apart of their own will.
- <a id="ev-V-0047"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, SE 10** — *The minute on the wall* (Cathair dhearg). The council minute that refuses the boundary wall runs to four lines. The fourth reads: 'They do not come south.' Five of the twelve councillors initial it; the other seven do not sign against it.
- <a id="ev-V-0048"></a>**8 an t-Iuchar, SE 10** — *The Allt an Àigh walk* (Allt an Àigh). The followers of Na Seann Spioradan keep their yearly walk to the holy well called Allt an Àigh in the east, whose water, the old tales say, brings fortune. The custodians of the Rite speak against the walk and do not forbid it.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2509"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, SE 10** — *The Cnoc ghorm church school opens its first term* (Cnoc ghorm). Nine boys sit the first term of the school raised inside the new church at Cnoc ghorm, taught the humans' tongue and the western reading of the scripture by a master brought up from Seann Skell. The letter reporting it to the council asks for nothing and is filed without debate.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0045"><em>The church school at Cnoc ghorm</em>, 29 an Giblean, SE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2510"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, SE 10** — *Seumas mac Coinnich Ghlais proposes a marked boundary* (Cathair dhearg). The councillor of the eastern custodian houses lays a map before the council and asks for a ditch and bank, with stones set at the mile, along the line where the settled shires meet the Tuathaich country, arguing that a boundary kept only in memory will not hold as both peoples' numbers grow.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0046"><em>The border wall proposed</em>, 11 an Cèitean, SE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2511"></a>**1 an Dàmhair, SE 10** — *The council lets the wall stand unbuilt* (Cathair dhearg). After two hours' debate on cost and custom, an old councillor says plainly that in eight years no Tuathaich has crossed where he was not wanted, and the room presses the boundary no further. No vote is taken; the proposal is simply not renewed by anyone present.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0046"><em>The border wall proposed</em>, 11 an Cèitean, SE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2512"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, SE 10** — *The minute on the wall signed by five, opposed by none* (Cathair dhearg). Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's four-line minute, ending in the sentence spoken against the wall, is initialled by five of the twelve councillors. The other seven enter no dissent. The Library keeps the sheet as the whole of the boundary's history: proposed, weighed, and left undrawn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0047"><em>The minute on the wall</em>, 9 an t-Ògmhios, SE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2513"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, SE 10** — *Gormshuil begins a book of her own* (Cathair dhearg). Keeping the blotted first draft of the wall's minute rather than burning it, the under-clerk pastes it into a small board-bound book bought without her clerk-master's knowledge and begins, that same evening, a private record of her own, the first of the volumes she keeps for the rest of her working life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0048"><em>The Allt an Àigh walk</em>, 8 an t-Iuchar, SE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2514"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, SE 10** — *Gormshuil walks to Allt an Àigh with her mother* (Allt an Àigh). Given a fortnight's leave for the first time in two years, the under-clerk walks the old road east with her mother, of an Old Spirits house, to drink at the holy well and add a stone to its cairn, lodging a night on the way at the walkers' hall of Achadh gharbh.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0048"><em>The Allt an Àigh walk</em>, 8 an t-Iuchar, SE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2515"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, SE 10** — *The walkers' ledger at Achadh gharbh* (Achadh gharbh). The keeper of the hall built for the well's pilgrims shows Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill her cracked-spined ledger of every walker's shire and name, its pages already holding travellers from better than twenty shires, north and south and east and west of the island together on the one road.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2516"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, SE 10** — *The mountain's yield passes the humans' own figure*. A surveyor's report tells the council, in the flat language such reports keep, that the mine's yield has come back to what it gave under the humans and, in the month just past, gone beyond it, the working unchanged in every particular but the hands the profit now fills.

## The Years SE 11 – 15

- <a id="ev-V-0049"></a>**11 an Gearran, SE 11** — *The walkers at Achadh gharbh* (Achadh gharbh). The walkers to Allt an Àigh lodge at Achadh gharbh on the way, and the village builds a long hall for them. The hall's keeper writes each walker's shire in a book, and by the end of the decade it holds names from fifty shires.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-2515"><em>The walkers' ledger at Achadh gharbh</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, SE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0050"></a>**15 an Cèitean, SE 11** — *The mine worked to the full again*. The mine's yield after the Severance comes up to what it gave under the humans, and then passes it. The working is the same as before. Only the profit goes to other hands.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-2516"><em>The mountain's yield passes the humans' own figure</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, SE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0051"></a>**23 an Cèitean, SE 11** — *The Sloc Mòr concession* (Achadh dhomhain). The Crown grants the working of the Sloc Mòr, the great shaft at Achadh dhomhain, to Uisdean mac Ùisdein of Cathair mhòr, whose house held an overseer's post under the humans. The Crown takes a fifth of the yield. The terms are the humans' terms with the names changed.
- <a id="ev-V-0052"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, SE 11** — *The night-shift kept* (Cnoc fhiadhaich). The council will not end the working of the vein by day and night that the humans ordered two generations before. The mountain is still given no season of rest. The custodians of the Rite enter a protest, and then bless the shafts.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2517"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, SE 11** — *The Sloc Mòr granted to Uisdean mac Ùisdein* (Cathair dhearg). Uisdean mac Ùisdein of Cathair mhòr, whose family held an overseer's post there under the humans, comes to the capital to put his name to the working of the great shaft at Achadh dhomhain, the terms copied almost word for word from the humans' own ledgers save the fifth now kept for the Crown.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0051"><em>The Sloc Mòr concession</em>, 23 an Cèitean, SE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2518"></a>**4 an Dùbhlachd, SE 11** — *A board is seated over the Sloc Mòr's grant* (Cathair dhearg). Three clerks and an engineer are set at a table in the council's own house at Cathair dhearg to see the mine's grant kept to its terms, answering to no name grander than the mountain itself, and it is to this small board, not the council, that Uisdean mac Ùisdein afterward sends his returns.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0052"><em>The night-shift kept</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, SE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2519"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, SE 11** — *Uisdean mac Ùisdein's first contract with the hewers* (Achadh dhomhain).
