Before the snow closes the high tracks, Uisdean mac Ùisdein rides north to set his name against the hewers' own at the shaft-head, the roster and the rates of pay carried over unaltered from the rolls the humans had kept, only the name at the head of the page now his own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0052"><em>The night-shift kept</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, SE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2520"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, SE 11** — *The council lets the night shift stand* (Achadh dhomhain). Asked whether the mountain, now the island's own, should be given the rest the humans never allowed it, the mine board's engineer answers that the very yield just reported depends on a shaft that never stands idle, and the council sets the question aside rather than decide it either way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0052"><em>The night-shift kept</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, SE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2521"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, SE 11** — *The custodians enter their protest against the unresting shaft* (Achadh dhomhain). The custodian houses of the vein carry down a half-page paper asking not that the night shift end, which they know is no longer the council's to give back, but only that their protest stand written, so that none after can say the old custom's breaking went unmarked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0052"><em>The night-shift kept</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, SE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2522"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, SE 11** — *Gormshuil reads the grant at the shaft-head* (Achadh dhomhain). Sent north with the council's own copy of the Sloc Mòr grant, Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill reads it aloud to the assembled hewers by lamplight in the winter cold, the custodians of the shaft standing apart in their grey coats while the words that answer their protest with silence are read over their heads.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0052"><em>The night-shift kept</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, SE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2523"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, SE 11** — *The custodians bless the shafts they could not close* (Achadh dhomhain). Once the grant is read, the four custodians of the vein walk to the pit-mouth and speak an old blessing over it, calling on the mountain to hold, to give, and in its own time to rest, before turning back without further word to the lamps that burn on through the falling dark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0052"><em>The night-shift kept</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, SE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0053"></a>**14 am Màrt, SE 12** — *The pit towns fill* (Muileann dhearg). Dia-thìrich families from the hungry east go to the vein-towns for wages. Muileann dhearg doubles in size within three years. Its hall of the druid school, shut since the humans' time, is taken for a hewers' lodging and twice enlarged in those same years.
- <a id="ev-V-0054"></a>**6 an Lùnastal, SE 12** — *Baile thais grows on the coal road* (Baile thais). At Baile thais the coal road from the central mountains comes down to the Abhainn uaine above the gulf, and the town takes in carters, inns and a ropewalk. Its people double in a decade, and it is given a shire court.
- <a id="ev-V-0055"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, SE 12** — *Raiders off Cathair gheal* (Spùinneadairean-mara). Ships that fly no flag, some manned by men who once served the human administration, begin to raid the coast off Cathair gheal in the north-west. The Tuathaich towns suffer first, and no one defends them.
- <a id="ev-V-0056"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, SE 12** — *The coal line reaches the Sloc Mòr* (Achadh dhomhain). The mended railway is carried up the valley to the pithead at Achadh dhomhain. The first coal train runs from the Sloc Mòr to Cathair dhearg in the kingdom's name, on the humans' rails.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2524"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, SE 12** — *Iain mac Ruairidh taken on as chainman* (Achadh dhomhain). Iain, a hewer's son of the hills, is taken on by Lachlann mac Iain Bhàin, the Mine Board's surveyor, to carry the chain and keep the faces' book at the Sloc Mòr. He is sworn to no guild, only entered on the Board's roll.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0053"><em>The pit towns fill</em>, 14 am Màrt, SE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2525"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, SE 12** — *The druid hall at Muileann dhearg becomes a lodging* (Muileann dhearg). As hungry families from the east crowd into the vein-towns, Muileann dhearg's shut druid hall is opened again, not for its old teaching but for pallets on its floor, and is twice enlarged within a few years to hold them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0053"><em>The pit towns fill</em>, 14 am Màrt, SE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2526"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, SE 12** — *Inns and a ropewalk at Baile thais* (Baile thais). The crossing at Baile thais, where the coal road meets the Abhainn uaine, fills with carters who stay the night and then keep families there; inns, stables and a ropewalk making the cages' hauling-rope grow up along the ford within the decade.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0054"><em>Baile thais grows on the coal road</em>, 6 an Lùnastal, SE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2527"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, SE 12** — *The raiders' first season off Cathair gheal*. Flagless ships work the water off Cathair gheal in the north-west; a fishing house is burned on the shore below Cathair gheal and two boats are lost from Cathair gheal's own harbour. The council's word, when it comes the next spring, is four lines asking that the matter be watched.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0055"><em>Raiders off Cathair gheal</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, SE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2528"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, SE 12** — *The first coal train runs to the capital* (Achadh dhomhain). On the third of an Dàmhair the mended rail carries the first train, loaded with coal cut that week, from the Sloc Mòr's pithead at Achadh dhomhain down to Cathair dhearg on the humans' own iron, a Tuathaich engineer at the footplate.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0056"><em>The coal line reaches the Sloc Mòr</em>, 3 an Dàmhair, SE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2529"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 12** — *The Mac Ùisdein quarry-mark first cut* (Achadh dhomhain). The grey, black-veined spoil of the Sloc Mòr's deeper galleries is quarried and dressed for building, and sold south under a stylised wave, the mark of the house of Mac Ùisdein, cut into every squared block.
- <a id="ev-V-0057"></a>**25 an Cèitean, SE 13** — *The quarry at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). The spoil of the Sloc Mòr, a grey stone veined with black, is cut and sold for building under the quarry-mark of the house of Mac Ùisdein. For forty years after it is used in public buildings across the south.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-EVI-2529"><em>The Mac Ùisdein quarry-mark first cut</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0058"></a>**8 an t-Iuchar, SE 13** — *The shunting yards at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). The Rail Board lays new sidings at Muileann chrom, where the coal trains from the Sloc Mòr are broken up and made up again for the ports. The families of the yard, who work the small engines that move the wagons, are counted apart by the Board and live apart in rows beside the lines.
- <a id="ev-V-0058a"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, SE 13** — *The western branch* (Seann Bhral). The Rail Board carries a branch of the coal line west from Cathair dhearg to the port of Seann Bhral, with a spur north to the pits at Àth leathan, so that the western workings may send their coal east by rail.
- <a id="ev-V-0059"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, SE 13** — *The guilds restored*. The old custom of binding apprentices, from the Holy Age, is taken up again in a changed form. It is now kept for Dia-thìrich alone.
- <a id="ev-V-0060"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, SE 13** — *The Guild of Hewers chartered* (Achadh dhomhain). The first guild under the restored custom, the Guild of Hewers, is chartered at Achadh dhomhain. Its oath is sworn with a hand on a piece of coal. By the charter its rolls are open to Dia-thìrich only.
- <a id="ev-EVI-2530"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, SE 13** — *The Rail Board's office raised at Cathair dhearg* (Achadh dhomhain). The Rail Board builds its office at Cathair dhearg, low and of the same grey Mac Ùisdein stone, and the Board's business, surveys among them, is thereafter kept within its walls.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0057"><em>The quarry at Achadh dhomhain</em>, 25 an Cèitean, SE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2531"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, SE 13** — *Lachlann mac Iain Bhàin's book of the faces* (Achadh dhomhain). Lachlann mac Iain Bhàin, the Mine Board's surveyor at the Sloc Mòr, keeps a running book of the faces he and his chainman measure, entering each true figure against the hewers who are paid by the fathom driven.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0053"><em>The pit towns fill</em>, 14 am Màrt, SE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2532"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, SE 13** — *The shunting yard at Muileann chrom counted apart* (Muileann chrom). New sidings at Muileann chrom, where the Sloc Mòr's coal trains are broken up and made up for the ports, bring rows of housing for the families who work the small engines. The Board keeps their roll separate from the shire's and houses them apart, beside the lines.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0058"><em>The shunting yards at Muileann chrom</em>, 8 an t-Iuchar, SE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2533"></a>**4 an Dùbhlachd, SE 13** — *The spur to Àth leathan opened* (Àth leathan). The Rail Board lays thirteen miles of new rail off the western branch to Àth leathan, where Tuathaich hewers have long worked the coal, judging the ground poor but the coal cheap to lift and the carters' road worse each winter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0058"><em>The shunting yards at Muileann chrom</em>, 8 an t-Iuchar, SE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2534"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, SE 13** — *The Guild of Hewers chartered at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). The restored custom of binding, kept now for Dia-thìrich alone, is set into the Guild of Hewers' charter and read aloud at Achadh dhomhain. Each hewer taken in lays a hand flat on a lump of coal and swears to keep the guild's custom, take no outside work and teach no craft of it to a hand unsworn.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0060"><em>The Guild of Hewers chartered</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, SE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-2535"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 13** — *Iain mac Ruairidh stands outside the oath* (Achadh dhomhain). At the guild's chartering Iain watches his own father sworn among the hewers and understands that the charter's rolls, open to those who cut, haul or timber the coal, hold no place for the Board's chainman who only measures where it lies.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0060"><em>The Guild of Hewers chartered</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, SE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0061"></a>**29 am Faoilleach, SE 14** — *The shipwrights of Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The shipwrights of Ros dhomhain take a guild charter of their own and bind their first thirty apprentices in a single day on the slipway.
- <a id="ev-V-0062"></a>**28 am Màrt, SE 14** — *The indentures broken* (Cuan shean). At Cuan shean and Seann Bhral the Tuathaich boys already bound to Dia-thìrich masters are loosed from their indentures under the charter rule. Some go north. Most stay on as day-labourers, outside the guilds and their wages.
- <a id="ev-V-0063"></a>**26 an Giblean, SE 14** — *The chandlers of Ceann àrsaidh* (Ceann àrsaidh). The ship-chandlers of Ceann àrsaidh, on the Abhainn fhionn east of the capital, take a guild charter and the sole right to supply the Crown's patrol boats. The right outlasts the boats.
- <a id="ev-V-0064"></a>**23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 14** — *The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin* (Muileann mhin). The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin, who make the coal lamps of every shaft on the island, are chartered as a guild. Their mark, a flame over a hammer, is stamped on every lamp. Of all the guild marks, the humans' traders copied this one only.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3000"></a>**24 an t-Ògmhios, SE 14** — *Harry Marlow's indenture torn at Cuan shean* (Cuan shean). Seumas Crùbach, shipwright of Cuan shean, takes down and tears the four-year indenture binding Harry Marlow to his yard, the guild court's charter rule having reached the coast that spring. He keeps Harry on the bench as a free hand rather than take a new bound apprentice in his place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0062"><em>The indentures broken</em>, 28 am Màrt, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3001"></a>**6 an t-Iuchar, SE 14** — *The Tuathaich day-wage set at the Cuan shean yard* (Cuan shean). Seumas Crùbach keeps Harry Marlow at half a bound man's wage and no guild standing once the indenture is loosed, a rate other yards along the coast take up that spring for the Tuathaich hands they keep on without a guild's leave to teach them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0062"><em>The indentures broken</em>, 28 am Màrt, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3002"></a>**18 an t-Iuchar, SE 14** — *A Tuathaich boy's plea refused at the Ros dhomhain guild court* (Ros dhomhain). A rope-maker's apprentice of four years' standing at Ros dhomhain brings his case to the newly chartered guild court and is heard and refused in a single sitting, the court ruling that the charter's custom of binding names Dia-thìrich hands alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0061"><em>The shipwrights of Ros dhomhain</em>, 29 am Faoilleach, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3003"></a>**30 an t-Iuchar, SE 14** — *The Moot's letter on the indentures filed* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr writes to the guild court at Cathair dhearg asking what is to become of the Tuathaich indentures already standing when the guilds' charters are read. The letter is filed among that year's business without an answer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0062"><em>The indentures broken</em>, 28 am Màrt, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3004"></a>**11 an Lùnastal, SE 14** — *The lamp-makers' mark first stamped* (Muileann mhin). The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin, chartered that winter, set their mark, a flame struck over a hammer, on every coal lamp leaving their sheds from that year on, so that the lamp itself carries the record of where it was made and under what oath.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0064"><em>The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3005"></a>**16 an t-Sultain, SE 14** — *The chandlers' patrol-boat right first exercised* (Ceann àrsaidh). The newly chartered chandlers of Ceann àrsaidh fit out the Crown's patrol boats under their sole right that spring, and the fitting-out becomes the guild's yearly show of its charter before the shire's maor.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0063"><em>The chandlers of Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 26 an Giblean, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3006"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, SE 14** — *Harry Marlow measures the old wreck at Cuan shean* (Cuan shean). Freed from bound hours by the loosing of his indenture, Harry Marlow spends the year's stolen hours setting down in his own book the full lines of a derelict human hull left on the Cuan shean hard, learning by his own measure how a hull built plank first and framed after is made to hold together.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0064"><em>The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3007"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, SE 14** — *A northern passage offered and refused at Cuan shean* (Cuan shean). A cloth trader out of Seann Vell, putting in at Cuan shean that autumn, tells Harry Marlow a free hand might do better in a northern harbour, where no guild court stands over a craftsman's work. Harry thanks him and stays at his bench.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0064"><em>The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3008"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, SE 14** — *Harry Marlow sends his wage north at half rate* (Cuan shean). At the year's end Harry Marlow sends north to his father Joseph Marlow's forge at Doire mhin the sum he has set aside from a free hand's half-wage, a smaller sum than any year of his bound apprenticeship, kept from the same habit regardless.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0064"><em>The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0065"></a>**6 am Faoilleach, SE 15** — *The weavers of Baile chiar* (Baile chiar). The weavers of Baile chiar are chartered as a guild. Their cloth of southern wool undersells the northern cloth at the fair, until the mills of Doire ghlas are built.
- <a id="ev-V-0066"></a>**14 am Faoilleach, SE 15** — *Agnes Pike's school* (Doire ghlas). Agnes Pike, a Tuathaich teacher, opens a school at Doire ghlas that teaches in the humans' tongue, with the Moot's money and without the council's leave. Within ten years there are nine such schools in the north. The council never licenses them and never shuts them.
- <a id="ev-V-0067"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, SE 15** — *The Cill ghlas district reopened* (Scàineadh Cill ghlas). The mining district shut since the Rending is surveyed and declared safe to work. On the surveyors' word the first new shafts are cut well back from the old fault line.
- <a id="ev-V-0068"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15** — *The Leòid circuit in the north* (Ceann mhòr). Eilidh nic Leòid rides the northern circuit for the first time and holds court at Ceann mhòr. Of the nineteen cases brought before her, seventeen are Tuathaich suits over land. In fifteen she finds for the Crown, citing her own ruling.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3009"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, SE 15** — *Baile chiar's weavers take a guild charter* (Baile chiar). The council's clerks cut a new seal, a shuttle over a fleece, for the weavers of Baile chiar, entering the grant in a book bound in calf at Cathair dhearg after a fee is paid and a feast given. It is a charter of the ordinary kind: coin changes hands, a form is followed, and a craft already practised becomes a craft the kingdom has agreed to notice.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0065"><em>The weavers of Baile chiar</em>, 6 am Faoilleach, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3010"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, SE 15** — *The Moot votes its school purse* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr sets aside money of its own for a schoolroom at Doire ghlas, without asking the council's leave a second time, Walter Hale having judged that a council which says no once will say no as often as it is asked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0032"><em>The Moot's schoolhouse petition</em>, 10 an Gearran, SE 7</a>; → Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0066"><em>Agnes Pike's school</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3011"></a>**17 an Lùnastal, SE 15** — *A widow lends her byre at Doire ghlas* (Doire ghlas). Jenny Marrow, whose husband's cattle a fever and a wet spring had thinned to a few head, offers her byre for the winter months in exchange for nothing but a promise that she and the children will be taught to write their names.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3012"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, SE 15** — *Walter Hale carries the school purse north* (Doire ghlas). Walter Hale rides the coast road himself to bring Agnes Pike the Moot's money the evening before her school opens, and leaves with it a sheet in his own hand setting out that the purse is the Moot's, the room the widow's, and the leave nobody's at all.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0066"><em>Agnes Pike's school</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3013"></a>**22 an Lùnastal, SE 15** — *Agnes Pike's school opens on the fourteenth of am Faoilleach* (Doire ghlas). Eleven children come through the byre door at Doire ghlas before the Church bell finishes its stroke, to be taught their letters from the Bible and from a lent volume of the Moot's own minutes, there being no primer printed for the humans' tongue on the island.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0066"><em>Agnes Pike's school</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3014"></a>**24 an Lùnastal, SE 15** — *The school's register begun* (Doire ghlas). Agnes Pike opens a register for the byre school in its first week, its first leaf recording eleven scholars and that no leave was asked for the room because none was thought likely to be given.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3015"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, SE 15** — *Daniel Frayne walks in from Muileann leathan* (Muileann leathan). A fisherman's son of nine walks the coast path each morning from Muileann leathan to sit on Agnes Pike's benches, and back again in time to help haul his father's nets, a condition he keeps every day the school runs that winter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0066"><em>Agnes Pike's school</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3016"></a>**15 an t-Sultain, SE 15** — *Daniel Frayne's fair copies pinned to the byre wall* (Doire ghlas). Slower at reading than at writing, the boy is set to copy out each day's psalm or minute a second time, and by the spring his fair copies, stroke for stroke exact, are pinned the length of the byre's one dry wall.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3017"></a>**16 an t-Sultain, SE 15** — *The maor visits the byre school and writes nothing* (Doire ghlas). The shire's maor, whose office is to note anything newly opened in it, rides out, watches the children recite a psalm, asks Agnes Pike only after the room's heating and the children's fees, and sends south that season a report of harvest, head-due and bridge that says nothing of the school at all.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-V-0066"><em>Agnes Pike's school</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3018"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, SE 15** — *Alice Hale opens a second school at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale's daughter Alice opens a school of her own in a disused net-store behind the harbour at Caol mhòr, on a purse thinner than her father carried north, and writes to Agnes Pike asking what has answered best on the byre's cold mornings.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-V-0066"><em>Agnes Pike's school</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3019"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, SE 15** — *The Cill ghlas fault line walked and found unmoved* (Scàineadh Cill ghlas). Lachlann mac Iain Bhàin and his chainman Iain mac Ruairidh trace the old Cill ghlas fault foot by foot with plumb and cord and file a report at Cathair mhòr declaring the district safe to work again so long as new shafts are cut a full chain back from it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0067"><em>The Cill ghlas district reopened</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3020"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, SE 15** — *The school moves to the church porch for summer* (Doire ghlas). With the widow's cattle wanting the byre back for the warm months, Agnes Pike's school moves into the porch of the Doire ghlas church, a change it makes every summer after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3021"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, SE 15** — *Daniel Frayne copies the minute of the school's own founding* (Doire ghlas). On the last morning before the move to the church porch, Agnes Pike sets her best copyist the Moot's own four-line minute recording the school's opening, and pins his fair copy into the register's first leaf rather than to the drying wall.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3022"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, SE 15** — *Eilidh nic Leòid opens the Ceann mhòr assize* (Ceann mhòr). In the heat of an t-Iuchar, with the windows of the old magistrate's house propped open against the fish-yard smell, Eilidh nic Leòid tells the crowded room that she will hear all nineteen causes on the list to their own ends, in their own order, whatever the likeness of one paper to the next, and whatever the weather asks of everyone waiting on the bench.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3023"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, SE 15** — *The Dunlop title read to its end* (Ceann mhòr). Eilidh nic Leòid reads a human grant brown at its folds, and a receipt for seed corn the family thought to bring unasked, and finds as she found seven years before at Seann Bhral: the ground is the Crown's, the working of it the Dunlops', on the same terms as before and no excusal from any due to come.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0038"><em>The Leòid ruling</em>, 10 an t-Sultain, SE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3024"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, SE 15** — *Fifteen suits found for the Crown at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). Cause after cause of the seventeen brought on human titles is decided in the words of the Leòid ruling, the ground passing to the Crown and the working of it staying with the family that holds it, until the room has learned, before the week is out, to stop guessing at an ending it already knows.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3025"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, SE 15** — *A custodian's countersign found on the Coombe title* (Ceann mhòr). In the margin of a Tuathaich family's human grant, Eilidh nic Leòid finds the pressed mark of an old land-keeping custodian, witness to the transfer in the humans' own time, and rules that a grant allowed also by an office of the island's own older law stands on ground the crossing never touched.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3026"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, SE 15** — *The Coombes and the Pettifers found for the holders* (Ceann mhòr). Two of the seventeen suits at Ceann mhòr, each carrying a custodian's old countersign on its title, are found whole for the families that hold them, the only two of the assize's nineteen causes decided against the Crown that summer.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3027"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, SE 15** — *Walter Hale heard as a witness at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). Having no standing to plead, Walter Hale is called instead to the bench as a witness, and shows Eilidh nic Leòid the Moot's own minute of a family's land divided by agreement and set down in writing years before, which the court accepts over the memory of the parties themselves.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0032"><em>The Moot's schoolhouse petition</em>, 10 an Gearran, SE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3028"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, SE 15** — *The Moot's minute-books credited by a Crown bench* (Ceann mhòr). Eilidh nic Leòid rules that a record kept by a body the Crown does not recognise is no less a fact for the hand that wrote it holding no seal, the first time the Moot's own paper is taken as evidence before a circuit justice.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3029"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 15** — *Hale and Eilidh nic Leòid speak at the Ceann mhòr inn* (Ceann mhòr). Over supper Walter Hale asks Eilidh nic Leòid whether an exact law can also be a fair one; she tells him plainly that she made her ruling to be exact rather than kind, and that she knows whose convenience it was written to serve, a thing she has told no maor and no council chest.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0068"><em>The Leòid circuit in the north</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3030"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 15** — *Eilidh nic Leòid begins the gathered book* (Cathair dhomhain). Through the winter after the Ceann mhòr sitting, Eilidh nic Leòid sets down in one book the whole of her nine years' rulings on Tuathaich land, from the Seann Bhral ruling to the seventeen suits, so that a justice after her need not dig the council's own chests to learn what she already knows.

## The Years SE 16 – 20

- <a id="ev-V-0069"></a>**2 an Giblean, SE 16** — *Eilidh nic Leòid dies* (Cathair dhomhain). Eilidh nic Leòid dies at Cathair dhomhain. Her rulings are bound in one book, the first law-book of the restored kingdom, and every circuit justice after her carries a copy.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVI-3030"><em>Eilidh nic Leòid begins the gathered book</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3031"></a>**10 an Giblean, SE 16** — *Eilidh nic Leòid sends for Uilleam mac Leòid* (Cathair dhomhain). Failing through am Màrt, Eilidh nic Leòid sends word north to her brother's son Uilleam, a young man who has ridden the northern circuit with her twice as a boy, asking him to take up the circuit she can no longer ride.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0069"><em>Eilidh nic Leòid dies</em>, 2 an Giblean, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3032"></a>**20 an Giblean, SE 16** — *Eilidh nic Leòid dies at Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). Eilidh nic Leòid dies in her own house within sound of the harbour, her clerk Murchadh Clàrc beside her and the gathered book of her rulings finished but not yet bound on the table by the bed.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0069"><em>Eilidh nic Leòid dies</em>, 2 an Giblean, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3033"></a>**27 an Giblean, SE 16** — *Leabhar nam Breith bound* (Cathair dhomhain). The council's own binder binds Eilidh nic Leòid's gathered rulings in plain calf under the name she chose for it herself, Leabhar nam Breith, and every circuit justice after her is given a copy to carry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0069"><em>Eilidh nic Leòid dies</em>, 2 an Giblean, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3034"></a>**29 an Giblean, SE 16** — *Uilleam mac Leòid named to the northern circuit* (Cathair dhomhain). Uilleam mac Leòid is named circuit justice of the north in his aunt's place, and rides for his first assize with Leabhar nam Breith strapped behind his clerk's saddle, as the satchel of blank record-books was once strapped behind his aunt's.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0069"><em>Eilidh nic Leòid dies</em>, 2 an Giblean, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0070"></a>**1 an Cèitean, SE 16** — *Leabharlann Muileann chaol founded* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). A great library is founded at Muileann chaol. In time it holds the fullest record of the island's past that has come down.
- <a id="ev-V-0071"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, SE 16** — *Ailean Leabhar, first keeper* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Ailean mac Iain, called Ailean Leabhar, is made the first keeper of Leabharlann Muileann chaol. He brings with him the council's minute-books and what is left of the humans' tithe ledgers, takes in the custodians' rolls kept in the town's cellars since the Severance war, and spends his first years having them read.
- <a id="ev-V-0072"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, SE 16** — *A chur san Leabharlann* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Within a few years 'a chur san Leabharlann', to put it in the Library, is said of anything settled beyond dispute. Ailean Leabhar is said to have disliked the phrase, for the Library settles nothing, he said, and only keeps.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3500"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, SE 16** — *Ailean mac Iain named first keeper of the Library* (Muileann chaol). By the council's own sentence, Ailean mac Iain is named keeper of the record at Muileann chaol, to receive, to order, and to keep whatever is sent to him. The office has no precedent and the warrant no further words, leaving Ailean to learn from the town itself what a keeper of a record might be.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0071"><em>Ailean Leabhar, first keeper</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3501"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, SE 16** — *The custodians' rolls found under Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). The town's own custodians lead Ailean Leabhar down a stair to a wet cellar under the old grain-store, where rolls and bound books have stood on planks above standing water since before the Severance, the lowest tier gone soft as bread. He reads three lines by the light thrown down the stair, then sends for lamps and a table.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0071"><em>Ailean Leabhar, first keeper</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3502"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, SE 16** — *Coinneach Clàrc taken on at the Library* (Muileann chaol). A wright's orphaned son of Muileann chaol, thirteen that spring and hired out by his mother for whatever a household could spare, attaches himself to Ailean Leabhar's carts on their first afternoon in the town and is set to fetch and carry, and within the year to read a Mission hand that few south of the guard-line can any longer make out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0072"><em>A chur san Leabharlann</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3503"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, SE 16** — *The council's minute-books sent east to the Library* (Muileann chaol). Four sacks of the council's own minute-books, and behind them the boxed and charred tithe ledgers of the humans' counting-houses that Ailean boxed unread fourteen years before, are carried east from Cathair dhearg to Muileann chaol, the first of the kingdom's scattered papers to be gathered into one keeping.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0071"><em>Ailean Leabhar, first keeper</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3504"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 16** — *The Library's first reading room opened* (Muileann chaol). Ailean Leabhar opens a dry chamber above the cellar to any who can show a letter from a shire maor vouching for their errand, on the plain reasoning that a Library nobody can reach is no better kept than a cellar nobody can reach. For the better part of a year it stands empty of anyone but his own copyists.
- <a id="ev-V-0073"></a>**30 an Cèitean, SE 17** — *The first readers* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The library's first reading room is opened to any who can show a letter from a shire maor. The first reader written in its book is a shipwright of Ros dhomhain, who asks for the humans' plans of their hulls.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-3504"><em>The Library's first reading room opened</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0074"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, SE 17** — *The bath-house at the hot springs* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). A new bath-house is built over the hot springs near Muileann ruadh, paid for by the Guild of Hewers for miners sick with the dust. The guild's sick-roll for its first year names four hundred men by name and shift.
- <a id="ev-V-0075"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, SE 17** — *The keepers of the five lights* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). The five lighthouses built under the humans are given Dia-thìrich keepers by royal warrant. At Taigh-solais Baile chrom on the Tuathaich coast the keeper is a Dia-thìreach man lodged in a Tuathaich town, and his warrant bids him report what he sees on land as well as at sea.
- <a id="ev-V-0076"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, SE 17** — *The Muileann chaol town grows* (Muileann chaol). Copyists, binders and paper-makers settle at Muileann chaol about the library. The town is granted a market charter, and its first market day is held in the library's yard.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3505"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, SE 17** — *The Library's copyists turn every date to the civil calendar* (Muileann chaol). Ailean Leabhar sets his copyists to turning every date the cellar and the tithe ledgers hold into the civil calendar the humans brought, disliking the old count of the Diosal, which runs backward into the thousands and names every year after the day the humans' kin went over the water.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0071"><em>Ailean Leabhar, first keeper</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3506"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, SE 17** — *The Age of Ailean parted from the eldest age* (Muileann chaol). Laying the tellings of Clann na Ceiste against the king-lists the custodians' rolls preserve, Ailean Leabhar's reckoners find that nearly half of the copyists' eldest age falls within the single life of Ailean Mòr, and by the consent of all seven copyists that life is counted an age of its own, the first change the Library makes to any reckoning it did not itself invent.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0071"><em>Ailean Leabhar, first keeper</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3507"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, SE 17** — *"A chur san Leabharlann" first said at Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). A council clerk, told that a boundary query will want weeks of reading before it can be honestly answered, says the matter can simply be put in the Library and left settled. Ailean Leabhar corrects him sharply, and the correction, carried home and retold, is what fixes the phrase in the town's mouth rather than loosening it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0072"><em>A chur san Leabharlann</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3508"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, SE 17** — *Cailean mac Eachainn's Line of Aisling found in the margin* (Muileann chaol). Copying a camp roll of Àth ìseal a third time, Coinneach Clàrc notices a second, later hand in its margin: Cailean mac Eachainn's line of descent, the Line of Aisling, set down a great many years before. Ailean Leabhar has it copied fair within the week.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0076"><em>The Muileann chaol town grows</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3509"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, SE 17** — *Leabhar nan Sloinnidhean opened* (Muileann chaol). Ailean Leabhar begins a book for nothing but lines of descent, naming it Leabhar nan Sloinnidhean, the book of lines, and sets Cailean mac Eachainn's Line of Aisling in it directly after the older Line of the Mason, found wedged behind a shifted course of brick in the same cellar.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0076"><em>The Muileann chaol town grows</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3510"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, SE 17** — *Leabhar nan Aithrisean opened* (Muileann chaol). Where the Àth ìseal roll's margin also keeps tales set down by firelight rather than by day, the Hollow Man, the white stag, a captain's boast of a wolf and a door held alone, Ailean Leabhar opens a second book, Leabhar nan Aithrisean, the book of tellings, and enters the long years of Ailean Mòr and his children beside them without correction.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0076"><em>The Muileann chaol town grows</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3511"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, SE 17** — *A Ros dhomhain shipwright first signs the reading-book* (Ros dhomhain). A shipwright of Ros dhomhain walks the coast road with a maor's letter to ask whether the humans ever set down the true lines of a hull. Ailean Leabhar finds three drawings folded inside an unrelated survey, and the shipwright copies them out over four days, the first name entered in the Library's reading-book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0073"><em>The first readers</em>, 30 an Cèitean, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3512"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, SE 17** — *The Guild of Hewers' bath-house built at the warm springs* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). The Guild of Hewers builds a bath-house of its own funds over the hot springs below Muileann ruadh, for men the pits have made sick with the dust, and sends the Library its first sick-roll unasked: four hundred men named by shift and by face of the pit that broke them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0074"><em>The bath-house at the hot springs</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3513"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, SE 17** — *The five lighthouses given Dia-thìreach keepers* (Muileann chaol). By royal warrant the five lighthouses built under the humans are given keepers of the kingdom's own naming. Ailean Leabhar drafts all five, the four southern warrants alike and the fifth, for Baile chrom on the Tuathaich coast, bidding its keeper report what he sees by land as well as by sea.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0075"><em>The keepers of the five lights</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3514"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, SE 17** — *The keeper's light lit at Baile chrom* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). A Dia-thìreach keeper who asked for the northern posting himself takes up the light at Baile chrom, among a Tuathaich town that has never before had a Dia-thìreach man set to live and watch among it. The southern four lights draw no comment; the fifth draws only silence that first season.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0075"><em>The keepers of the five lights</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3515"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, SE 17** — *Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill sent to inspect the Library at Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). The council sends its under-clerk Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill, four-and-forty, to see and report on the record Ailean Leabhar has kept these four years at Muileann chaol, the errand falling to her only for want of causes on her own desk that month.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0071"><em>Ailean Leabhar, first keeper</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, SE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3516"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, SE 17** — *Muileann chaol granted a market charter* (Muileann chaol). The district's maor writes up, at the keeper's own asking, that a town which has drawn copyists, binders and paper-makers to it in four years without leave might as well be given a charter before its own trade sets its rules instead. The council grants it in the usual form, a fee for every stall and a court to hear the fair's disputes.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-V-0076"><em>The Muileann chaol town grows</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3517"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 17** — *The first market day held in the Library's yard* (Muileann chaol). Thirty stalls of thread, nails, candles and the district's own produce are set up on trestles against the Library's wall, the stall-fee a penny a table paid into a box the keeper's boy carries, and the fair's own court amounting to the boy's mother settling disputes over table-space in a voice heard the length of the yard.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0076"><em>The Muileann chaol town grows</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3518"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 17** — *The Tobar dhìreach mill's first delivery reaches the Library* (Tobar dhìreach). Forty quires of the new paper-mill's paper are carried up the road on a borrowed cart, better and cheaper, by the copyists' own judgement, than anything the council's stationers at Cathair dhearg have sent north; within the year near enough every sheet the Library uses comes from the one stream.
- <a id="ev-V-0077"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, SE 18** — *The paper-mill at Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). A paper-mill is built at Tobar dhìreach, a few miles from the library, on the stream below the village. For half a century nearly every page of the royal chronicle is written on its paper.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-3518"><em>The Tobar dhìreach mill's first delivery reaches the Library</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0078"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, SE 18** — *The first royal chronicler appointed* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). An office is made to keep the records of the kingdom. From it comes the archive whence these annals are drawn.
- <a id="ev-V-0078a"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, SE 18** — *The years counted by the ages* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). With the office of chronicler the council orders that the kingdom's records shall count their years no longer by the Diosal but by the ages of the library's table, each age from its own first event: six ages as the table then stands, and seven since the Dubhan Era. The chronicler's first year is entered as the eighteenth of the Severance Era. Thereafter the count of the Diosal is kept only in old books.
- <a id="ev-V-0079"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, SE 18** — *Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The first royal chronicler is Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill, a clerk of the council. She keeps her record at Muileann chaol and not at the capital, and writes in her first entry that a record kept beside the throne is kept for the throne.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3519"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 18** — *The office of royal chronicler set at Muileann chaol, not the capital* (Muileann chaol). Sworn into the new office at Cathair dhearg and given no instruction as to its seat, Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill writes back within the week that she means to keep the record at Muileann chaol, beside the Library that already holds the rolls and the copyists the work wants, and that a record kept beside the throne is kept for the throne.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0079"><em>Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, SE 18</a>; ○ Same place <a href="#ev-V-0078"><em>The first royal chronicler appointed</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, SE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0080"></a>**25 am Màrt, SE 19** — *The first chronicle circuit* (Àth àrsaidh). Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill sends clerks to every shire to copy parish books, grave-lists and harbour rolls. The returns from the south fill forty chests. The returns from Siorrachd Àth àrsaidh and the other northern shires fill one, for few Tuathaich will speak to the clerks.
- <a id="ev-V-0080a"></a>**2 an Giblean, SE 19** — *The town arms copied* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The clerks of the first chronicle circuit copy the seal of every town they visit into the roll of arms, and the roll comes to hold the arms of five hundred and five places. In the north most are copied from the humans' old town seals, for few Tuathaich will show the clerks their own.
- <a id="ev-V-0081"></a>**11 an Cèitean, SE 19** — *The chest from Inis bheag* (Inis bheag). At Inis bheag in the north-east the chronicle clerks are shown a parish book that goes back before the coming of the humans, kept in the Seann Spioradan house there. The keeper lets it be copied, and not taken.
- <a id="ev-V-0082"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, SE 19** — *Boats lost off Cuan bheag* (Cuan bheag). A storm out of the west drowns eleven Tuathaich fishermen off Cuan bheag in the north. The village has no lifeboat. The Moot buys one by subscription and asks the council to pay half; the council pays a third.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3520"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, SE 19** — *Tormod mac Sheumais joins the first chronicle circuit* (Muileann chaol). A council under-clerk's son of three-and-thirty, called already Tormod Pinn for the speed of his hand, asks Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill for a place on the first circuit rather than wait to be sent, and rides the northern half of it.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-V-0080"><em>The first chronicle circuit</em>, 25 am Màrt, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3521"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, SE 19** — *The town arms of five hundred and five burghs copied into one book* (Muileann chaol). The chronicle circuit's southern chests yield the town arms of every burgh that has ever cut a seal, five hundred and five of them, entered by Coinneach Clàrc in the order the chests happen to arrive rather than by rank, on Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's own ruling that a tidied record forgets how untidy its own arrival was.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0080"><em>The first chronicle circuit</em>, 25 am Màrt, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3522"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, SE 19** — *The chronicle clerks turned away at Doire ghlas* (Doire ghlas). Tormod mac Sheumais reads the circuit's own warrant twice aloud in the street at the harbour agent's demand before he is let copy a single ledger; eleven of the town's twelve doors stay closed against him, an answer he judges memory rather than unkindness.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0080"><em>The first chronicle circuit</em>, 25 am Màrt, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3523"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, SE 19** — *The Inis bheag keeper lets his parish book be copied and not carried* (Inis bheag). The old keeper of the Seann Spioradan house at Inis bheag hears the circuit's warrant once, without asking it twice, and lets his parish roll be copied at his own table under his own eye, but will not let the book itself travel so much as to the harbour, telling the clerk that a book kept that many generations belongs to the house and not to any seal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0081"><em>The chest from Inis bheag</em>, 11 an Cèitean, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3524"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, SE 19** — *The northern chest opened: the maor's returns and nothing more* (Muileann chaol). Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill opens the one chest the northern shires have filled and finds only the maor of Siorrachd Àth àrsaidh's own tallies and licences, not a line in it written by a Tuathaich hand; she enters the fact plainly and adds no further word to it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0080"><em>The first chronicle circuit</em>, 25 am Màrt, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3525"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, SE 19** — *Thomas Coyle drowned off Cuan bheag* (Cuan bheag). A westerly storm on the second night of an t-Sultain drowns eleven Tuathaich fishermen out of Cuan bheag, Thomas Coyle of Caol mhòr among them, one-and-forty and near twenty years married to Mary Coyle. The sea gives back two broken hulls and a stranger's oar; the town buries what it can within the week.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0082"><em>Boats lost off Cuan bheag</em>, 28 an t-Sultain, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3526"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, SE 19** — *Mary Coyle's roll of the eleven dead* (Cuan bheag). Mary Coyle, newly widowed, writes the eleven drowned men's names out on a single sheet for the mason's stones, setting them in the order the boats went out rather than the order the sea gave the bodies back, holding that order the truer one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0082"><em>Boats lost off Cuan bheag</em>, 28 an t-Sultain, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3527"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, SE 19** — *The Moot opens its lifeboat subscription* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale carries the wreck's news to the Moot's own council at Caol mhòr, which votes that same evening to open a subscription for a lifeboat at Cuan bheag; Hale opens the list himself, and it carries near two hundred names by the month's end. The council, asked to bear half the cost, answers four months on that it will bear a third.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0082"><em>Boats lost off Cuan bheag</em>, 28 an t-Sultain, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3528"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, SE 19** — *The tale of the Sea-Watcher told to the chronicler* (Achadh àrsaidh). A fisherman out of Achadh àrsaidh, at the summer bothies below the cold cape, tells the royal chronicler Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill the coast's own tale of a shape seen off the cold cape, seen always at a distance and never named by those who fear it, which she enters in the book that keeps what people said rather than the book that keeps names.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3529"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, SE 19** — *The raiders' anchorage noted at the cold cape* (Uilebheist na Mara). The same fisherman tells Gormshuil that the flagless ships working those waters know the cold cape's currents better than any stranger crew should, and keep some hidden anchorage among its rocks; she writes it apart from the tale and asks that the council's coastal watch be told of it.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3530"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 19** — *The flocks of Eilean dhubh counted by their own hands* (Eilean dhubh). A treasury clerk sent to number the flocks of Eilean dhubh for the head-due finds the islanders unwilling to have him count their own pastures, and takes instead their sworn count by tally-stick, on which the island's dues are set that year and every year after.
- <a id="ev-V-0083"></a>**9 an Gearran, SE 20** — *The thing off the north-west cape* (Uilebheist na Mara). Fishermen out of Achadh àrsaidh tell of a creature longer than their boats in the waters off the north-west cape. Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill writes down the tale, and adds that the raiders shelter in those same waters.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-3528"><em>The tale of the Sea-Watcher told to the chronicler</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, SE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-3529"><em>The raiders' anchorage noted at the cold cape</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0084"></a>**10 am Màrt, SE 20** — *The Eilean dhubh sheep-count* (Eilean dhubh). A royal clerk is sent to count the flocks of Eilean dhubh, greatest of the outer isles, to set the island's dues. The islanders count them for him, and the dues are set on their count.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-3530"><em>The flocks of Eilean dhubh counted by their own hands</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0085"></a>**8 an Giblean, SE 20** — *Cathair gheal arms its boats* (Cathair gheal). The Tuathaich fishermen of Cathair gheal arm their own boats and drive the raiders from the bay. Twice they had asked the council for help, and none was sent. Afterwards the council fines the town for bearing arms without licence, and the fine is paid.
- <a id="ev-V-0086"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, SE 20** — *The market cross at Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). A market cross is raised at Cathair mhòr at the cost of the house of Mac Ùisdein, with the house's name cut on all four faces. The town's wool and coal markets are moved to its foot.
- <a id="ev-EVI-3531"></a>**24 an t-Sultain, SE 20** — *The Cuan bheag lifeboat launched* (Cuan bheag). The lifeboat ordered of the Cuan shean yard comes up the coast in an Cèitean and is set afloat off Cuan bheag's jetty by the hands of that autumn's five widows, no priest of either faith having an agreed form to bless a boat neither had built.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0082"><em>Boats lost off Cuan bheag</em>, 28 an t-Sultain, SE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3532"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, SE 20** — *Nell Barrow's first letter for Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). Nell Barrow, a skipper's widow of Cathair gheal who has lost a nephew to the raiders, writes the town's case to the council in am Faoilleach, asking a boat armed at the council's expense or leave to arm the town's own; the maor warns her plain words are as likely filed as answered. No answer comes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0085"><em>Cathair gheal arms its boats</em>, 8 an Giblean, SE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3533"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, SE 20** — *Nell Barrow's second letter for Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). Two months unanswered, Nell Barrow writes a second letter in am Màrt, shorter and plainer than the first, ending that the town does not think a third asking will find the council less occupied than the first two were. It too goes unanswered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0085"><em>Cathair gheal arms its boats</em>, 8 an Giblean, SE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3534"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, SE 20** — *The black ship run aground in Cathair gheal's bay* (Cathair gheal). On the night of 8 an Giblean three flagless hulls stand into Cathair gheal's bay; the largest raider ship runs her keel onto a shifted bar and is boarded and burned by seven town boats before dawn, the two lesser hulls standing off rather than come to her aid.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0085"><em>Cathair gheal arms its boats</em>, 8 an Giblean, SE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3535"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, SE 20** — *Two dead and four hurt in the bay's clearing* (Cathair gheal). The fight for Cathair gheal's bay costs the town two men dead and four hurt, one of whom keeps no further use of a hand; Nell Barrow herself takes a burn from a fallen lantern that scars her the rest of her life, and by first light tells the town the bay is clear.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0085"><em>Cathair gheal arms its boats</em>, 8 an Giblean, SE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3536"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, SE 20** — *Cathair gheal fined for bearing arms unlicensed* (Cathair gheal). The council's ruling on the night's fight names no boat sent and no licence granted, only that Cathair gheal bore arms without leave first asked, and fines the town forty pounds in the realm-coin, to be paid at the maor's own office before the year's dues fall due.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0085"><em>Cathair gheal arms its boats</em>, 8 an Giblean, SE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3537"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, SE 20** — *Walter Hale carries the Moot's purse north to Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). Hearing the town lacks two-thirds of its fine, Walter Hale carries the difference north from the Moot's own purse, the same purse the Cuan bheag lifeboat has already thinned, and reaches Cathair gheal near the end of an t-Iuchar.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0085"><em>Cathair gheal arms its boats</em>, 8 an Giblean, SE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-3538"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 20** — *The fine paid at the maor's door* (Cathair gheal). Nell Barrow's sum and Hale's together clear the fine in full at the maor's own door, counted coin by coin before his clerk, who enters the sum received and asks nothing of the six years, the two letters, or the boat the town was never sent.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0085"><em>Cathair gheal arms its boats</em>, 8 an Giblean, SE 20</a>.</span>

## The Years SE 21 – 25

- <a id="ev-V-0087"></a>**7 an Cèitean, SE 21** — *The house of the Stone at Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). The house of Òrd na Cloiche at Caol leathan, greatest of the order, is rebuilt with a tower, and a bell rings the hours from it. The town sets its market and its courts by the bell.
- <a id="ev-V-0088"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, SE 21** — *Fèill Muileann òg first held* (Fèill Muileann òg). A fair is held each year at Muileann òg, and it becomes the greatest gathering on the island. Trade comes to it from every province the state holds.
- <a id="ev-V-0089"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, SE 21** — *Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules* (Fèill Muileann òg). Oighrig nic Mhathain, first toll-mistress of the fair at Muileann òg, sets its rules: a stall-fee in coin, a court of the fair for disputes, and Tuathaich goods to be sold only through Dia-thìrich factors. The rules are read aloud at the opening of every fair to this day.
- <a id="ev-V-0090"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, SE 21** — *The fair's road* (Dùn chrom). The road from Cathair dhearg to Muileann òg is widened and metalled for the carts of the fair. It passes Dùn chrom, which takes a toll at its gate and grows on it. As far as Muileann ghlas it runs on the old coal road; the new stretches are called Rathad na Fèille.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4000"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, SE 21** — *The Stone's house at Caol leathan rebuilt* (Caol leathan). The order of the Stone rebuilds its house at Caol leathan at its own cost, raising a bell tower over the western gable; the town sets its market and its two courts by the bell from that year on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0087"><em>The house of the Stone at Caol leathan</em>, 7 an Cèitean, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4001"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, SE 21** — *Oighrig nic Mhathain named toll-mistress* (Dùn chrom). Oighrig nic Mhathain, nine years the market clerk of Dùn chrom and one-and-thirty that year, is asked by the council's eastern factor to keep the new fair to be held at the ford by Muileann òg, and takes the post, leaving her own scales to a niece she has trained two summers at her elbow.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0089"><em>Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4002"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, SE 21** — *The fair-field marked out at Muileann òg* (Fèill Muileann òg). Oighrig nic Mhathain walks the ground at Muileann òg with a length of cord and a stick through the summer, marking the stalls, the beast-pens and the corner where a court might sit, before any building has been raised there.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0088"><em>Fèill Muileann òg first held</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4003"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, SE 21** — *The court of the fair roofed* (Fèill Muileann òg). Carpenters of Dùn chrom finish a plain roofed frame, open on three sides, at the field's corner nearest the ford, a fortnight before the fair is to open; it is the only building the state gives the fair in its first year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0088"><em>Fèill Muileann òg first held</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4004"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, SE 21** — *Oighrig writes the fair's three rules* (Fèill Muileann òg). Over three evenings by rush-light Oighrig nic Mhathain writes the fair's rules in her own plain hand: a stall-fee in coin, a court of the fair to sit each day of the gathering, and Tuathaich goods to be sold only through licensed Dia-thìreach factors, on the council's own instruction.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0089"><em>Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4005"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, SE 21** — *The first factors licensed for northern goods* (Fèill Muileann òg). The council licenses four merchant houses of the eastern shires to stand factors' stalls at Muileann òg and sell Tuathaich goods under their own names for a share of the price; Oighrig nic Mhathain enters their names under a heading of her own, Bàillidhean na Fèille.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0089"><em>Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4006"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, SE 21** — *The court of the fair's first sitting* (Fèill Muileann òg). On the fair's opening morning, 16 an Dàmhair, Oighrig nic Mhathain's court hears its first case, a dispute over a barrel of salt fish, and settles it within the hour by weighing the barrel herself; she writes it into her book as setting the pattern for every case after it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0088"><em>Fèill Muileann òg first held</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4007"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, SE 21** — *The spoil-stone case judged by a smith's eye* (Fèill Muileann òg). A Cathair mhòr coal-carter brings a Sloc Mòr merchant's load of spoil-stone dressed to pass for coal-iron before the court of the fair; Oighrig nic Mhathain, having no forge of her own, sends the load to Muileann òg's one smith and fines the merchant by his judgment.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0088"><em>Fèill Muileann òg first held</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4008"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, SE 21** — *David Hale's wool turned away at the gate* (Fèill Muileann òg). David Hale of Caol mhòr brings four sacks of his father's wool to the fair's ninth day, the first cart from the Moot's own provinces to try it; Oighrig nic Mhathain reads him her own third clause and turns him to a factor's stall, where his wool sells for some fifth part less than a northern market would have given.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0089"><em>Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0091"></a>**2 an Lùnastal, SE 22** — *Dùn chrom's gate-toll* (Dùn chrom). The toll taken at Dùn chrom's gate on the fair road pays for a new wall on the town's southern side. The townsfolk call it the fair's wall. The carters of the fair call it something else.
- <a id="ev-V-0092"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, SE 22** — *Niall dies; Brìghde crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Niall dies, and his daughter Brìghde follows him without contest: a mortal heir passing to a mortal heir among a nobility some of whom never age. It was thought no wonder then. It was thought one later.
- <a id="ev-V-0093"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, SE 22** — *The chronicler's use of the saying* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill writes that the succession came 'mar a thàinig Niall'; it is the first time the saying is found in the royal record. In all her years as chronicler she lets no other idiom into the chronicle.
- <a id="ev-V-0094"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, SE 22** — *The ancestors' hall at Seann Dunn* (Seann Dunn). The Seann Spioradan houses of the east coast build a common hall at Seann Dunn, where each year the living heads of forty families name their ancestors aloud. The next year the list is copied to the library, and it grows by a few names every year after.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4009"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, SE 22** — *The fair's road metalled past Dùn chrom* (Dùn chrom). In am Faoilleach the last stretch of the road from Cathair dhearg to Muileann òg is metalled for the fair's carts; the carters already call it Rathad na Fèille before the state gives it a name of its own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0090"><em>The fair's road</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4010"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, SE 22** — *Dùn chrom's gate-toll raises the fair's wall* (Dùn chrom). The toll taken at Dùn chrom's gate on the fair's road pays, that same winter, for a new wall along the town's southern side, finished by an Cèitean; the townsfolk call it the fair's wall, and the carters call the gate by another name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0091"><em>Dùn chrom's gate-toll</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4011"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, SE 22** — *The Moot's letter against the factor rule filed* (Cathair dhearg). Walter Hale writes to the council on the Moot's behalf naming the factor rule a licence laid across a trade the north carried on unaided, and asks it looked at again; the council answers, months on, that the rule stands and will not be reconsidered inside the year, and the letter is filed with the Moot's earlier ones.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0089"><em>Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4012"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, SE 22** — *The fair's rules confirmed and read aloud* (Fèill Muileann òg). In an Lùnastal a council clerk reads Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules aloud before the gathered factors and maoir of the eastern shires, word for word as she wrote them, and asks whether the reading matches her own book; she tells him it does.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0089"><em>Oighrig nic Mhathain's rules</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, SE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4013"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, SE 22** — *The bells rung for Niall* (Cathair dhearg). The bells of Òrd Mhacha at Cathair dhearg are rung a full day and a night for Niall's death, and the capital keeps no market. The crowd that gathers is the largest since his crowning; it stays quiet, and disperses before the second night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0092"><em>Niall dies; Brìghde crowned</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4014"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22** — *The council's oath sworn afresh* (Cathair dhearg). The council of twelve, sitting on its fixed day within the week of the crowning, swears its oath of service afresh before Brìghde. The minute-book gives it one line among the day's ordinary business and no more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0092"><em>Niall dies; Brìghde crowned</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4015"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22** — *The corrected proclamation at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). A harbour clerk at Ros dhomhain, copying the crowning's proclamation for the gate, writes Niall's name from habit, scores it through, and sets Brìghde's above the line. The corrected copy is kept under glass at the gate.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0092"><em>Niall dies; Brìghde crowned</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4016"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22** — *Gormshuil's struck drafts* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The chronicler writes and rejects three entries for the crowning before any stands: one too bare, one that says more than an office should say first, one left unfinished as an argument rather than a record. All three are struck through in her working book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0093"><em>The chronicler's use of the saying</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4017"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22** — *Gormshuil's resolve on the one idiom* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Having let *mar a thàinig Niall* into the royal record, the chronicler resolves to admit no other such phrase for as long as the office is hers, having seen other offices lose their plainness one borrowed ornament at a time.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0093"><em>The chronicler's use of the saying</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4018"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22** — *The hall raised at Seann Dunn* (Seann Dunn). Forty households of the Seann Spioradan along the east coast raise a common hall at Seann Dunn in a single season, working the stone by day, and roof it before the first frost. It holds no image or carving, only two hearths.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0094"><em>The ancestors' hall at Seann Dunn</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4019"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22** — *Gormshuil's visit to the first naming* (Seann Dunn). The chronicler rides east to Seann Dunn to watch the hall's first naming of ancestors, not on the Library's business but her own, her mother's house keeping the same rite at a hearth too small for half its dead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0094"><em>The ancestors' hall at Seann Dunn</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4020"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22** — *The Library's offer to Seann Dunn* (Seann Dunn). Asked by an elder of the hall whether the Library keeps such lists of the dead, Gormshuil answers that it does not, but will keep any copy sent to it as carefully as anything else that reaches Muileann chaol.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0094"><em>The ancestors' hall at Seann Dunn</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4021"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22** — *The vote for a light at Cuan ruadh* (Cuan ruadh). After two boats are lost on the harbour rocks in a winter fog, the town council of Cuan ruadh votes its own coal money to burn a light on the mole where no Board light has ever reached.
- <a id="ev-V-0095"></a>**25 an Gearran, SE 23** — *Cuan ruadh's harbour light* (Cuan ruadh). Cuan ruadh on the east coast, which has none of the five lighthouses, raises a harbour light of its own on the mole and burns in it coal bought by the town. The Lighthouse Board will not take it on.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4021"><em>The vote for a light at Cuan ruadh</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0096"></a>**4 am Màrt, SE 23** — *Còmhrag Ceann leathan first fought* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). A fierce melee is first fought at Ceann leathan, and is fought there every year after. It is held to be a martial custom. More and more it is where a people with few other outlets spend their anger.
- <a id="ev-V-0097"></a>**22 an Lùnastal, SE 23** — *Calum Ruadh* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). The first champion of the Còmhrag whose name is remembered is Calum mac Aonghais, called Calum Ruadh, a hewer of Muileann chrom. Two men die in the melee he wins. The prize is a year's wages and the right to bear arms in any shire.
- <a id="ev-V-0098"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, SE 23** — *Ceann leathan's inns* (Ceann leathan). Ceann leathan builds four new inns for the crowds of the Còmhrag. The fair-wardens of the town, who take a share of every room, become the Còmhrag's keepers in all but name.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4022"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, SE 23** — *The Seann Dunn list first copied to the Library* (Seann Dunn). The hall at Seann Dunn sends the Library the first copy of its naming, and goes on sending one every year after, each a little longer than the last. Gormshuil enters only the day it came and the count of names.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0094"><em>The ancestors' hall at Seann Dunn</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, SE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4023"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, SE 23** — *The Lighthouse Board's refusal* (Cuan ruadh). The Comhairle nan Taighean-solais writes back to Cuan ruadh that its charter names five lights and no more, and that the town's own light, being no charge on the Crown, may continue as it is. Gormshuil enters the refusal in four lines.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0095"><em>Cuan ruadh's harbour light</em>, 25 an Gearran, SE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4024"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, SE 23** — *The rules of the first Còmhrag* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). The first Còmhrag at Ceann leathan is fought under rules that run to little more than a fee, a bar on edged weapons, and a purse for the last man standing inside the ropes. Nobody thinks the custom will need more than that.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0096"><em>Còmhrag Ceann leathan first fought</em>, 4 am Màrt, SE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4025"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, SE 23** — *The dead of the first Còmhrag buried* (Ceann leathan). Two men who do not walk out of the ropes at the first Còmhrag are buried at Ceann leathan within the week. The melee is fought again the following summer regardless, and the record gives their deaths one plain sentence.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0096"><em>Còmhrag Ceann leathan first fought</em>, 4 am Màrt, SE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0097"><em>Calum Ruadh</em>, 22 an Lùnastal, SE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4026"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, SE 23** — *Calum Ruadh's purse counted out* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). A year's wages are counted out on a trestle table by the fair-wardens' own clerk for Calum mac Aonghais, hewer of Muileann chrom, who wins the first Còmhrag by refusing to stay down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0097"><em>Calum Ruadh</em>, 22 an Lùnastal, SE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4027"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 23** — *The right to bear arms entered on the shire's roll* (Ceann leathan). Calum Ruadh's right to bear arms in any shire of the kingdom, the Còmhrag's second prize, is entered that same evening on the shire's roll at Ceann leathan, a right his own father never held.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0097"><em>Calum Ruadh</em>, 22 an Lùnastal, SE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4028"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, SE 23** — *The fair-wardens' free table* (Ceann leathan). The inn-keepers of Ceann leathan, four of whom built new houses that year for the Còmhrag's crowds, keep Calum Ruadh's table free of charge, a custom nobody formally agrees to but that holds for as long as he comes back to fight.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0098"><em>Ceann leathan's inns</em>, 30 an Lùnastal, SE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0099"></a>**10 am Màrt, SE 24** — *The grain-ships of Ros gheal* (Ros gheal). Ros gheal on the north-central coast builds a dock for the grain-ships of the Hawk country. The Hawk houses bless the dock and ask a tithe of its dues. The shire gives them a twentieth.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4029"></a>**11 an Cèitean, SE 24** — *Mary Coyle first speaks in the Moot* (Caol mhòr). Mary Coyle, widowed of the Cuan bheag drowning, stands and speaks her own words in the Moot at Caol mhòr rather than sending a note forward to be read by another. The clerk David Hale sets her speech down whole in the day-book, the first time a woman's words are kept there entire rather than summed in a line.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0099"><em>The grain-ships of Ros gheal</em>, 10 am Màrt, SE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0100"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, SE 24** — *Splatter and Dodge's generation born*. Many children are born in these years to the shunting families of the yard. From them come Seachran and Brean and others of that generation, who grow up to be Dubhan's closest allies.
- <a id="ev-V-0101"></a>**6 an t-Iuchar, SE 24** — *Seann Bhral in the south* (Seann Bhral). Seann Bhral on the south coast, not the town of that name in the west, becomes the greatest fishing port of the kingdom and lands more fish than Ros dhomhain. Its curing-sheds run the length of the harbour.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4030"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, SE 24** — *The widows heard first* (Caol mhòr). The Moot resolves that the widows of the drowned be heard on the same footing as any man who has paid his shilling, and heard first when a matter touches their own dead. The rule is entered as standing, not as a courtesy for one night, on the widow Agnes Tulloch's motion.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0099"><em>The grain-ships of Ros gheal</em>, 10 am Màrt, SE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4031"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, SE 24** — *The Hawk's twentieth first paid* (Ros gheal). Ros gheal's factor pays the Hawk houses their first quarter's twentieth on the dues of the new grain dock, the sum the shire's factor haggled down from a tithe. The due is paid every quarter after, and the clerks of Ros gheal come to call it simply the Hawk's, few remembering why.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0099"><em>The grain-ships of Ros gheal</em>, 10 am Màrt, SE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0102"></a>**4 an Lùnastal, SE 25** — *The circus at Seann Chwen* (An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn). The travelling show that calls itself An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn is first recorded, pitched near Seann Chwen on the southern coast. The chronicler's clerk could not say what its acts were meant to show. Nor, he adds, could the crowd, and it came back the next night.
- <a id="ev-V-0103"></a>**2 an t-Sultain, SE 25** — *Manannan's feast at Seann Bhral* (Seann Bhral). The house of Òrd Mhanannain at Seann Bhral, one of the oldest on the west coast, will not admit the Tuathaich from the north who come to its feast of the sea, as their forebears learned to do from the Dia-thìrich harbours. Its keeper says the sea is the same and the house is not.
