- <a id="ev-EVI-4032"></a>**16 an t-Sultain, SE 25** — *The Moot votes to send the western crossing* (Caol mhòr). After two hard sittings the Moot agrees to Mary Coyle's asking, that northern boats sail west-about to keep the sea-feast at Seann Bhral where the Tuathaich forebears once kept it. Many in the room call it a fool's errand for winter, and are not silenced, only outvoted.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0103"><em>Manannan's feast at Seann Bhral</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, SE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4033"></a>**18 an t-Sultain, SE 25** — *Eleven boats sail for Seann Bhral* (Caol mhòr). Eleven boats out of Caol mhòr, Cuan bheag and Achadh àrsaidh put out on a frozen morning under Mary Coyle, carrying little but themselves, a keg of salt fish apiece, and the Moot's own sheet naming her their word. Ros bheag's harbour will not give them its quay, and sends them to a mooring buoy instead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0103"><em>Manannan's feast at Seann Bhral</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, SE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4034"></a>**20 an t-Sultain, SE 25** — *A boat nearly lost off the passage*. A squall out of the south-west puts green water over the bow of the smallest boat of the eleven, and its crew bails her clear with whatever will hold water. No one of the fleet is lost on the four days' passage, though more than one aboard call it the hardest going since the Crossing itself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0103"><em>Manannan's feast at Seann Bhral</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, SE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4035"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, SE 25** — *The house at Seann Bhral answers Mary Coyle* (Seann Bhral). The keeper of Manannan's order at Seann Bhral in the west hears Mary Coyle's asking through to the end and refuses it: the house is kept on tithes of families who hold the rite by blood and the custodian's book, and cannot be opened on a four days' claim, however justly sailed. He tells her the sea is the same; the house is not.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0103"><em>Manannan's feast at Seann Bhral</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, SE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4036"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, SE 25** — *Mary Coyle resolves to keep the feast at Cnoc ghorm* (Cnoc ghorm). On the passage home Mary Coyle tells the crews the north will keep the feast of the sea itself, in full, at the church above Cnoc ghorm where a thin blessing of the boats is already kept each spring. The decision is made before the eleven boats raise Caol mhòr again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0103"><em>Manannan's feast at Seann Bhral</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, SE 25</a>.</span>

## The Years SE 26 – 30

- <a id="ev-V-0104"></a>**11 an Gearran, SE 26** — *The northern sea-feast* (Cnoc ghorm). Turned away at Seann Bhral, the Tuathaich keep the feast at the church at Cnoc ghorm instead, as a blessing of the boats. They keep it there every year after, and within a generation the northern feast is greater than the western.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4036"><em>Mary Coyle resolves to keep the feast at Cnoc ghorm</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, SE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4037"></a>**15 an Gearran, SE 26** — *The first Fleadh na Mara kept in full* (Cnoc ghorm). More than fifty boats gather at Cnoc ghorm on the second Sunday of an Gearran, far beyond any year before, and the parish priest blesses each hull in turn with heather dipped in harbour water. Mary Coyle's own boat, which carried her to Seann Bhral and back, is blessed fourth in the row.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0104"><em>The northern sea-feast</em>, 11 an Gearran, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4038"></a>**10 am Màrt, SE 26** — *David Hale counts the boats at Cnoc ghorm* (Cnoc ghorm). David Hale keeps a written count of the boats blessed at Cnoc ghorm for the Moot's day-book, the first such count taken of the feast. Word of the gathering's size travels the north coast faster than the crossing to Seann Bhral had, and boats are promised from as far as Inis mhin's country the year after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0104"><em>The northern sea-feast</em>, 11 an Gearran, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0105"></a>**12 am Màrt, SE 26** — *The Depletion first noted*. The survey reports begin to note, without remark, that the vein yields less. For years the state does nothing.
- <a id="ev-V-0106"></a>**9 an Cèitean, SE 26** — *Iain Mapa's survey* (Achadh dhomhain). The survey behind the report is the work of Iain mac Ruairidh, called Iain Mapa, of the Mine Board. His measures of the faces of the Sloc Mòr show the vein thinning to east and south. The Board files the survey and shows it to no one, and Iain Mapa is sent to the silver works at Muileann chiar.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4500"></a>**20 an t-Ògmhios, SE 26** — *Iain Mapa true up the eastern faces* (Achadh dhomhain). Sent into the eastern galleries of the Sloc Mòr to settle a dispute between two overseers over a cutting's bounds, the chainman Iain mac Ruairidh, called Iain Mapa, checks an old survey against the new digging and finds the figures will not lie flat. He walks the faces a second time before he trusts what they tell him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0105"><em>The Depletion first noted</em>, 12 am Màrt, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4501"></a>**2 an Lùnastal, SE 26** — *The vein found thinning east and south* (Achadh dhomhain). A third survey of the faces gives Iain Mapa the same figures as the first two, to within an inch the chain itself can account for: the vein runs narrower to the east than the old maps show, and pinches again to the south. He sets it down in a hand that does not shake, and does not argue.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0105"><em>The Depletion first noted</em>, 12 am Màrt, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4502"></a>**9 an Lùnastal, SE 26** — *Iain Mapa walks the survey to Cathair dhearg* (Achadh dhomhain). Rather than trust the carters with a finding he believes the Board should see in his own hand, Iain Mapa rolls and ties his survey and walks the thirty-one miles from the Sloc Mòr to Cathair dhearg in a day and a half, sleeping one night on the road, and tells no one at the mine beforehand what the sheet holds.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0106"><em>Iain Mapa's survey</em>, 9 an Cèitean, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4503"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, SE 26** — *The Board leaves the survey unrolled* (Cathair mhòr). Iain Mapa lays his survey before three men of the Mine Board at Cathair dhearg and unties the string himself. None of the three unrolls it. He gives them the finding by mouth, plainly, and is told only, by the one in the middle, that it will be considered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0106"><em>Iain Mapa's survey</em>, 9 an Cèitean, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4504"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, SE 26** — *Ruairidh mac Ailein signs the receipt* (Cathair mhòr). Asked for a receipt for the survey he has carried in, Iain Mapa is given four written lines naming nothing of the finding, only that a survey was received and filed. Ruairidh mac Ailein of the Board signs it, since the man in the middle will not, and Iain Mapa folds it into his pocket-book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0106"><em>Iain Mapa's survey</em>, 9 an Cèitean, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4505"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, SE 26** — *The survey filed and shown to no one* (Cathair mhòr). Within the week Iain Mapa's survey is filed in the Board's own press at Cathair dhearg with the two years' surveys before it, and circulated to no one on the council or in any other office of the state. It lies there unread while the men who might have acted on it go on believing the mountain gives as freely as ever.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0106"><em>Iain Mapa's survey</em>, 9 an Cèitean, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4506"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, SE 26** — *Iain Mapa posted to Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar). Within the month Iain Mapa is told, with little explanation offered and none asked for, that he is wanted at the silver works at Muileann chiar, twenty-four miles east and a little south of the Sloc Mòr, where the Board has need of a man who holds a chain straight and asks no more than the work requires.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0106"><em>Iain Mapa's survey</em>, 9 an Cèitean, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4507"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 26** — *The boat of the field warped into the new harbour* (Cuan dhearg). Of the hulls the Great Wave cast into the fields behind Cuan dhearg two generations before, one is found sound enough to be dragged to the water, caulked and floated, and is warped into the rebuilt harbour ahead of every boat built new for it. The harbour-master keeps it moored at the quay-head as a relic rather than putting it back to work.
- <a id="ev-V-0107"></a>**4 am Faoilleach, SE 27** — *The Mine Board at Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). The Mine Board, which has sat at Cathair dhearg since the Sloc Mòr concession, moves its clerks to Cathair mhòr to be nearer the mountain. By the Board's own rule its surveys are kept there and not sent to the library.
- <a id="ev-V-0107a"></a>**15 an Gearran, SE 27** — *The scent-makers of Seann Vell* (Seann Vell). The glass-houses of the capital shore begin to make small flasks, and in them the women of Seann Vell sell the waters they distil from bog-myrtle, meadowsweet and heather honey. Within a few years scent is sold in every market town, and the towns of the western plain take up the trade.
- <a id="ev-V-0108"></a>**15 an t-Ògmhios, SE 27** — *The Grey Night forbidden* (Baile chrom). A Dia-thìreach magistrate at Baile chrom forbids the gatherings of the Grey Night sect as disorderly. Hannah Crane is fined. The vigil goes indoors and goes on.
- <a id="ev-V-0109"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, SE 27** — *The harbour at Cuan dhearg reopened* (Cuan dhearg). The harbour at Cuan dhearg, lost to the Great Wave, is opened again with a new mole of dressed stone. The first boat in is one of those found in the fields behind the old town, refloated, and kept by the harbour-master as a relic.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4507"><em>The boat of the field warped into the new harbour</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 26</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4508"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, SE 27** — *The Board's clerks move to Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). The Mine Board moves its clerks and its presses the sixteen miles from Cathair dhearg to Cathair mhòr, into leased rooms above the town's wool market, on the stated ground that a board charged with the mountain's business ought to sit nearer the mountain than it had.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0107"><em>The Mine Board at Cathair mhòr</em>, 4 am Faoilleach, SE 27</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4509"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, SE 27** — *Riaghailt a' Bhùird set down* (Cathair mhòr). In four lines the Mine Board sets down, for the first time in writing, the rule that its surveyors' work is to be kept at Cathair mhòr in the Board's own presses and not sent to the Library at Muileann chaol as every other office's reports are sent. No one on the council is asked to confirm it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0107"><em>The Mine Board at Cathair mhòr</em>, 4 am Faoilleach, SE 27</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4510"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, SE 27** — *The Moot pays Hannah Crane's fine* (Baile chrom). Word reaches the Moot at Caol mhòr that the vigil-keeper Hannah Crane has been fined at Baile chrom for keeping the Grey Night in the open. The Moot votes the balance of her fine out of its own small chest without much debate, on a councillor's motion that a woman fined for standing on a beach is no threat worth agreeing with.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0108"><em>The Grey Night forbidden</em>, 15 an t-Ògmhios, SE 27</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4511"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, SE 27** — *The Grey Night kept indoors* (Baile chrom). Forbidden the open shingle below the light, the vigil of the Grey Night is kept that year in a byre lent by a family who hold the old rite themselves, one night a year, in a silence the magistrate's order cannot reach any better than it reached the shore. Outsiders are still not told which night it falls on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0108"><em>The Grey Night forbidden</em>, 15 an t-Ògmhios, SE 27</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4512"></a>**5 am Faoilleach, SE 28** — *Achadh mhin's old bounds restored* (Achadh mhin). The shire measures the returning households of Achadh mhin back onto the same strips the humans' surveyors once cut, the old plat being the one the families still walk by memory rather than a new line drawn by a Dia-thìreach chain.
- <a id="ev-V-0110"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, SE 28** — *Achadh mhin resettled* (Achadh mhin). The fields of Achadh mhin bear again, and a few of the families moved away after the Great Wave come back to them. The shire gives them their old bounds from the humans' survey.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4512"><em>Achadh mhin's old bounds restored</em>, 5 am Faoilleach, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0111"></a>**11 an Gearran, SE 28** — *Eòghan crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Brìghde dies young, and no cause is made known. Her cousin Eòghan takes the throne, and for the first time the restored kingdom's succession is in dispute.
- <a id="ev-V-0112"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, SE 28** — *The succession entry* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The royal chronicler's entry for the succession gives the bare fact. The chroniclers after Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill have added nothing to it.
- <a id="ev-V-0113"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *Dissent recorded in council* (Cathair dhearg). For the first time the council's minutes record votes against a succession. They name the councillors who voted, and not their reasons. Two of them do not sit again.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4513"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *The first households return to Achadh mhin* (Achadh mhin). Three households moved off the salted fields after the Great Wave, or their children in their place, ask and are granted their old ground back, the barley coming up along strips long thought lost to the tide.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0110"><em>Achadh mhin resettled</em>, 13 am Faoilleach, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4514"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *The twice-sealed packet reaches Muileann chaol* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Word of Brìghde's death and Eòghan's crowning reaches the chronicler's desk in a packet sealed twice, the second hand adding, in a hastier line at the foot, that the council's own sitting on the succession did not pass as quietly as the crowning itself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0111"><em>Eòghan crowned</em>, 11 an Gearran, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4515"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *Gormshuil's three struck drafts* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The chronicler writes and rejects three entries for the succession before a fourth stands: one that says more than an office should say first, one so bare it reads as a door shut on purpose, one left unfinished as an argument rather than a record.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0111"><em>Eòghan crowned</em>, 11 an Gearran, SE 28</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0112"><em>The succession entry</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4516"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *The bare entry set down* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Past the second hour of the morning Gormshuil enters the day of Brìghde's death, the fact that no cause is made known, and the day of Eòghan's crowning, and nothing more, choosing the silence rather than dressing it as a fullness it is not.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0112"><em>The succession entry</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4517"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *The council's four lines on the division* (Cathair dhearg). The council's own minute of the sitting names Tormod mac Iain Òig and Sìleas nic Artair as the two who stood against seating Eòghan, gives no reason either offered, and closes with the plainest of its four lines: the two do not sit again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0113"><em>Dissent recorded in council</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4518"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *Tormod mac Iain Òig goes home* (Cathair dhearg). Tormod mac Iain Òig returns to his own lands in the western shires and is not named in the chronicle again for some years, his seat on the council closed behind him without further entry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0113"><em>Dissent recorded in council</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4519"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *Sìleas nic Artair keeps her own house's rite*. Sìleas nic Artair, her council seat lost with Tormod mac Iain Òig's, gives her Old Spirits kin's house more of her time than council business ever left her, and does not sit at Cathair dhearg again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0113"><em>Dissent recorded in council</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4520"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28** — *The council's two seats filled* (Cathair dhearg). Before the year turns the council seats a landed man's son from the western shires and a widow of a coastal house in the two empty places, and neither newcomer is asked in council to account for the vote that opened the seat they now hold.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0113"><em>Dissent recorded in council</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, SE 28</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4521"></a>**10 an Gearran, SE 29** — *The warehouse quarter of Inis bhàn burns two days* (Inis bhàn). Fire takes three storehouses and the dwellings above them at Inis bhàn on the Abhainn ìseal and burns two days before the town beats it back street by street with buckets and wet sacking; every soul in the burning quarter gets clear, and none dies.
- <a id="ev-V-0114"></a>**12 am Màrt, SE 29** — *Inis bhàn's fire* (Inis bhàn). Fire takes the warehouse quarter of Inis bhàn on the Abhainn ìseal in the north-central country and burns for two days. The town's Hawk house takes in the homeless. The fire-bell the town buys afterwards is the loudest in the kingdom.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4521"><em>The warehouse quarter of Inis bhàn burns two days</em>, 10 an Gearran, SE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0115"></a>**9 an Cèitean, SE 29** — *Dubhan born*. Dubhan is born mortal, in the north where the Severance confined his people, decades after the war that shut the island against those from whom his line descends.
- <a id="ev-V-0116"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, SE 29** — *The Tuathaich schools counted* (Doire ghlas). The Moot counts eleven schools in the north that teach in the humans' tongue, and three that have begun to teach Dia-thìris as well, at the parents' asking. Agnes Pike's school at Doire ghlas is one of the three.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4522"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, SE 29** — *The Hawk house at Inis bhàn opens its doors* (Inis bhàn). The Hawk house at Inis bhàn, which has never before taken in households outside those sworn to it, shelters every family the fire puts out of a roof, sworn or not, through the worst of the spring cold.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0114"><em>Inis bhàn's fire</em>, 12 am Màrt, SE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4523"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, SE 29** — *Inis bhàn's new bell rung on the quay* (Inis bhàn). The council buys Inis bhàn a bell from the founders' yard at Cathair dhearg to stand where the old warehouse bell burned, rung once on the quay before it is hung, and heard, by the town's own telling, further up and down the Abhainn ìseal than any bell in the kingdom.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0114"><em>Inis bhàn's fire</em>, 12 am Màrt, SE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4524"></a>**24 an Dàmhair, SE 29** — *The Moot's letter of the eleven schools* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale writes the Moot's count of the north's schools to Muileann chaol, eleven in all from Agnes Pike's byre at Doire ghlas to a room over a chandler's shop at Ceann àrsaidh opened that same autumn, and Gormshuil enters it whole rather than shortened.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0116"><em>The Tuathaich schools counted</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, SE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4525"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, SE 29** — *Three schools begin teaching Dia-thìris*. At three of the north's eleven schools the teachers begin, at the parents' own asking and with no order from the council or leave from any maor, to teach Dia-thìris alongside the humans' letters, so that children may read a proclamation or a boundary-line in the tongue the kingdom writes its business in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0116"><em>The Tuathaich schools counted</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, SE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4526"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, SE 29** — *Agnes Pike's school teaches its first Dia-thìris lesson* (Doire ghlas). Agnes Pike's school at Doire ghlas, one of the three the Moot's letter names, sets its first Dia-thìris lesson beside the Bible and the Moot's own minutes, at the asking of the parents whose children it has taught since its founding.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0116"><em>The Tuathaich schools counted</em>, 7 an t-Ògmhios, SE 29</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0117"></a>**10 an Giblean, SE 30** — *The stone house of Mac Ùisdein* (Cathair mhòr). Uisdean mac Ùisdein's house at Cathair mhòr is rebuilt in stone quarried from the spoil of the Sloc Mòr, the greatest private house in the kingdom. The Guild of Hewers holds its feast in the new hall.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4527"></a>**27 an Giblean, SE 30** — *The Guild of Hewers feasts in the new hall* (Cathair mhòr). The Guild of Hewers holds its feast in the finished stone hall of Uisdean mac Ùisdein at Cathair mhòr, at tables set the length of the room under torches an ironsmith made to no pattern but his own, and Mòrag nic Coinnich attends as the Library's own witness.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0117"><em>The stone house of Mac Ùisdein</em>, 10 an Giblean, SE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0118"></a>**26 an Cèitean, SE 30** — *The northern fishing grounds* (Caol mhòr). Licences to fish the waters south and east of Caol mhòr are kept for Dia-thìrich boats. The Tuathaich boats are left the northern grounds, where the raiders also fish.
- <a id="ev-V-0119"></a>**24 an t-Ògmhios, SE 30** — *Doire shean's harbour* (Doire shean). Doire shean in the south-west builds a stone harbour for the fishing boats of the Stone's country, the first new harbour since the Severance not paid for by the Crown. The house of the Stone lends the money and takes the harbour dues.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4528"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, SE 30** — *The mason's letter of the hall he did not sit in* (Cathair mhòr). A mason who dressed the stone of Mac Ùisdein's new hall writes the Library that he was not asked to the guild's own feast in it, his craft holding no sworn place for a cutter of stone, and Ailean Leabhar enters the letter whole rather than in his own shorter hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0117"><em>The stone house of Mac Ùisdein</em>, 10 an Giblean, SE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4529"></a>**15 an Dàmhair, SE 30** — *The first licence refused to a Caol mhòr boat* (Caol mhòr). Coll, a Tuathaich master who has fished the southern banks off Caol mhòr eleven years, brings his catch to the maor's scales the day the new licences take force and is told the grounds are not, at present, being papered for boats of his fleet; the Moot enters the day and his name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0118"><em>The northern fishing grounds</em>, 26 an Cèitean, SE 30</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4530"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, SE 30** — *The house of the Stone takes its first quarter's dues* (Doire shean). The house of the Stone at Doire shean takes its first quarter's harbour dues off the new quay before the mole's last course is dry, the sum entered beside what the house first lent the town for the building of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0119"><em>Doire shean's harbour</em>, 24 an t-Ògmhios, SE 30</a>.</span>

## The Years SE 31 – 35

- <a id="ev-V-0120"></a>**3 an Giblean, SE 31** — *Trenches at Làrach an Dùin* (Làrach an Dùin). Diggers sent by the library open trenches at Làrach an Dùin on the south-east coast. They find walls older than any Dia-thìreach building, and no writing at all. Ailean Leabhar has the finds entered as of the Old Ones, purpose unknown.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4531"></a>**25 an Giblean, SE 31** — *Beathag asks that the temple's ground be left* (Làrach an Teampaill). Beathag, eldest of three Seann Spioradan elders of the district, meets Ailean Leabhar at Làrach an Teampaill and asks that the Library measure the ruin rather than open it, since whatever lies under the stone is neither hers to claim nor his.
- <a id="ev-V-0121"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, SE 31** — *Làrach an Teampaill measured* (Làrach an Teampaill). The library's diggers measure the ruin called Làrach an Teampaill in the east and do not dig it, at the asking of the Seann Spioradan houses of the district. The keeper enters it as measured and let be.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4531"><em>Beathag asks that the temple's ground be left</em>, 25 an Giblean, SE 31</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4532"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, SE 31** — *The diggers' camp opens at Làrach an Dùin* (Làrach an Dùin). Four diggers under a foreman named Cailean cut trenches through the spring above the headland at Làrach an Dùin, following the line of a coursed wall sunk deeper than any footing they have found the bottom of.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0120"><em>Trenches at Làrach an Dùin</em>, 3 an Giblean, SE 31</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4533"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, SE 31** — *Ailean Leabhar rides to the trenches* (Làrach an Dùin). The keeper of the Library goes down himself to Làrach an Dùin on the diggers' word that the wall they have found is older than any ruin the Library holds a record of, and spends four days at the trench's edge with a lamp and a notebook.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0120"><em>Trenches at Làrach an Dùin</em>, 3 an Giblean, SE 31</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4534"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, SE 31** — *The finds laid in the Library* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Ailean Leabhar carries the season's three findings, the wall's short entry, the measure of Làrach an Teampaill, and the copied obelisk, into the Library's own presses himself, filing the not-knowing of each as carefully as a certainty.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0120"><em>Trenches at Làrach an Dùin</em>, 3 an Giblean, SE 31</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0121"><em>Làrach an Teampaill measured</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, SE 31</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4535"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, SE 31** — *Ailean measures the temple with a chain, not a spade* (Làrach an Teampaill). Ailean Leabhar spends two days at Làrach an Teampaill setting down the line of the fallen wall and the fall of the ground with a chain and a level, and enters the ruin as measured, and let be.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0121"><em>Làrach an Teampaill measured</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, SE 31</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4536"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, SE 31** — *Una copies the obelisk stroke by stroke* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). Una, a scribe trained under Ailean Leabhar in copying the Library's most damaged leaves, spends three weeks of fair days at the foot of the obelisk near Cnoc bheag setting down every stroke of its unread script exactly as the stone gives it, worn gap for worn gap.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4537"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, SE 31** — *The council pays for a fence at the obelisk* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). On the keeper's word that a stone unread for longer than the kingdom's whole span deserves at least a fence against the cattle, the council finds the money for four posts and a rail set well back from the obelisk's foot.
- <a id="ev-V-0122"></a>**29 am Màrt, SE 32** — *The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied* (Carragh Cnoc bheag). A scribe of the library copies the writing on the obelisk near Cnoc bheag, stroke by stroke. It is like no script known on the island. The copy is filed and the obelisk fenced.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4534"><em>The finds laid in the Library</em>, 22 an t-Samhain, SE 31</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4536"><em>Una copies the obelisk stroke by stroke</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, SE 31</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4537"><em>The council pays for a fence at the obelisk</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, SE 31</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4538"></a>**23 an Giblean, SE 32** — *The keeper of Baile chrom's lighthouse reports the vigil* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). A Dia-thìrich keeper new to the lighthouse at Baile chrom reports the Grey Night sect's yearly vigil kept silent in the tower's own shadow, and makes no move against it, having no order that names a silent watch on open ground his business.
- <a id="ev-V-0123"></a>**27 an Giblean, SE 32** — *A lighthouse on the Tuathaich coast* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). The Dia-thìreach keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom reports to the council that the Grey Night sect keeps its vigil in the dark of the lighthouse's own shadow. The council does nothing.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4538"><em>The keeper of Baile chrom's lighthouse reports the vigil</em>, 23 an Giblean, SE 32</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0124"></a>**26 an Cèitean, SE 32** — *Salt-pans of Àth bheag* (Àth bheag). Salt-pans are dug on the flats below Àth bheag on the east coast, and within a few years the town supplies the whole eastern seaboard. The salt goes inland by the old drove road past Baile ìseal.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4539"></a>**22 an t-Iuchar, SE 32** — *The council answers the keeper's report with nothing* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). No order reaches the keeper of Baile chrom's lighthouse, and no word reaches the magistrate who had once fined the vigil in the open, and Ailean Leabhar enters the council's silence into the Library's register as plainly as any finding.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0123"><em>A lighthouse on the Tuathaich coast</em>, 27 an Giblean, SE 32</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4540"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, SE 32** — *Mòrag nic Coinnich made Ailean's deputy* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). On the road home from Àth bheag, Ailean Leabhar asks Mòrag nic Coinnich to stand as the Library's deputy after a season that has taught him one keeper alone is a Library one bad season from having nobody who can speak for it; she agrees, on the condition that the register always name her deputy and never keeper.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0124"><em>Salt-pans of Àth bheag</em>, 26 an Cèitean, SE 32</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0125"></a>**1 am Faoilleach, SE 33** — *Cathair fhada's grain-store* (Cathair fhada). Cathair fhada on the southern plain builds a Crown grain-store great enough to feed the south for a season. It is filled from the south's own harvests, and first opened in the dry years at Achadh shean.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4541"></a>**10 am Faoilleach, SE 33** — *The grain-store at Cathair fhada opens its doors* (Cathair fhada). In the dry weeks of a poor season the keeper of the new Crown grain-store walks out to the road and tells the first cart that passes that the south will eat that year whatever the sky withholds, and word of the opened doors outruns, by an evening, word of how bad the year will prove.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0125"><em>Cathair fhada's grain-store</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0126"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, SE 33** — *The second census after the Severance*. The second census measures for the first time how far the Tuathaich live below the Dia-thìrich; until now it was only seen. The report is not made public.
- <a id="ev-V-0127"></a>**28 an Gearran, SE 33** — *Walter Hale dies* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale, first speaker of the Moot, dies at Caol mhòr. The Moot chooses Mary Coyle, a fisherman's widow, to follow him, the first woman to hold the chair.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4542"></a>**4 am Màrt, SE 33** — *The second census rides the shire roads*. Clerks sent out a second time from Cathair dhearg tally hearth against hearth as before, but with a new column set beside the first, a figure for what a Dia-thìreach household holds and one for what its Tuathach neighbour holds, so that the count for once measures the gap rather than only setting the numbers side by side.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0126"><em>The second census after the Severance</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4543"></a>**9 am Màrt, SE 33** — *The council locks the second census away* (Cathair dhearg). The sums the shire clerks carry back to Cathair dhearg go onto a stack in the council's own keeping-room and no further; no proclamation, no minute copied to the Library, no word to any shire clerk who might have carried it on, and the twelve who asked for the count give out only that the figures want study before they want airing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0126"><em>The second census after the Severance</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4544"></a>**9 an Giblean, SE 33** — *Walter Hale settles a carter's toll dispute* (Caol mhòr). Keeping the thirty-year habit of hearing the furthest-travelled petitioner before the day's set business, Walter Hale hears out a carter from beyond Àth fhada over a wrongly charged toll and settles it in the carter's favour himself, his voice unhurried though the sitting leaves him more spent than harder business had the winter before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0127"><em>Walter Hale dies</em>, 28 an Gearran, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4545"></a>**28 an Giblean, SE 33** — *Walter Hale dies at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). Walter Hale, first speaker of the Moot, dies in his own bed at Caol mhòr on the twenty-eighth of an Gearran, seventy-six years old, David beside him and Alice sent for but not in time; the Moot's business stops three days without a vote taken to stop it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0127"><em>Walter Hale dies</em>, 28 an Gearran, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4546"></a>**3 an Cèitean, SE 33** — *The north walks to Hale's burial* (Caol mhòr). Fishermen, carters and shepherds from every part of the north crowd the roads into Caol mhòr for Walter Hale's burial, more feet on the road that week than the fair itself drew the autumn before, and he is laid in sight of the Moot's own house where he sat thirty-one years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0127"><em>Walter Hale dies</em>, 28 an Gearran, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4547"></a>**3 an t-Ògmhios, SE 33** — *The Moot names Mary Coyle speaker* (Caol mhòr). On the fourth day after Hale's burial the Moot sets aside a factor's son and a shire clerk both spoken for the chair and names Mary Coyle, a fisherman's widow of Caol mhòr, the first woman to hold it, by a count nobody in the room troubles to call close.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0127"><em>Walter Hale dies</em>, 28 an Gearran, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4548"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, SE 33** — *David Hale keeps the books under Mary Coyle* (Caol mhòr). David Hale, who kept his father's minute-books through the years of the first fair, sets Mary Coyle's seal at her own place beside the one his father's hand had set to thirty-one years of letters, and stays on at her asking to keep the rough book as he always has.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0127"><em>Walter Hale dies</em>, 28 an Gearran, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4549"></a>**27 an t-Ògmhios, SE 33** — *Seonag nic Ille-Mhoire asks to see the report* (Cathair dhearg). Seonag nic Ille-Mhoire, who rode her own shire's tally in for the second census, asks a council clerk at Cathair dhearg to let her see the island's whole sum, on the ground that she carried the figures herself and has a right to know their total.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4550"></a>**28 an t-Iuchar, SE 33** — *Seonag writes the refusal into her own book*. Refused the report with no reason beyond the plain fact of the refusal, Seonag nic Ille-Mhoire writes the asking and the answer that same evening into a private book she keeps for herself and shows to no one, for a record's own sake rather than any purpose she could name.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4551"></a>**16 an Lùnastal, SE 33** — *Ruth Ashby and Clara Tulloch begin under Eachann mac Rath* (Àth àrsaidh). Two women of the shunting country north of Caol mhòr, Ruth Ashby and Clara Tulloch, come to the surgery of Eachann mac Rath at Àth àrsaidh, who takes them without his guild's leave to be taught by watching him set bones and mix poultices through a hard, fever-crowded season.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4552"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, SE 33** — *The guild's men find Eachann's surgery out* (Àth àrsaidh). Word from a factor's wife reaches the physicians' guild that Eachann mac Rath's two new pupils handle a lancet as steady as he does, and two of the guild's own men ride to Àth àrsaidh and watch Ruth Ashby set a child's wrist unwatched before they leave without a word to either woman.
- <a id="ev-EVI-4553"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, SE 33** — *Eachann mac Rath struck from the physicians' guild* (Àth àrsaidh). The guild strikes Eachann mac Rath from its rolls before an Cèitean is out, its letter naming no fault in his physic, only that he taught outside its leave and to hands its charter does not recognise, and he sets the letter aside and keeps his surgery open all the same.
- <a id="ev-V-0128"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, SE 34** — *The census clerks' private note* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Seonag nic Ille-Mhoire, one of the census clerks, leaves among her papers a note that she asked to see the report on the gap and was refused. The note came to the library with her papers after her death. It is the only mention of the report outside the council.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4549"><em>Seonag nic Ille-Mhoire asks to see the report</em>, 27 an t-Ògmhios, SE 33</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4550"><em>Seonag writes the refusal into her own book</em>, 28 an t-Iuchar, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0129"></a>**11 an Gearran, SE 34** — *The Tuathaich doctors* (Àth àrsaidh). The Moot pays for two Tuathaich women to be taught medicine by a Dia-thìreach physician at Àth àrsaidh, who takes them against the will of his guild. He is struck from its rolls. They practise in the north for forty years.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4551"><em>Ruth Ashby and Clara Tulloch begin under Eachann mac Rath</em>, 16 an Lùnastal, SE 33</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4552"><em>The guild's men find Eachann's surgery out</em>, 21 an t-Sultain, SE 33</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4553"><em>Eachann mac Rath struck from the physicians' guild</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, SE 33</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4554"></a>**26 an Gearran, SE 34** — *The Abhainn ìseal takes three bridges and the embankment* (Abhainn ìseal). Three days of hard rain in am Màrt bring the Abhainn ìseal over its lower banks, and the flood carries away three bridges and a long stretch of the coal line's embankment, a carter losing his cart on the middle span but no soul drowned along that reach.
- <a id="ev-V-0130"></a>**12 am Màrt, SE 34** — *The Abhainn ìseal floods* (Abhainn ìseal). The Abhainn ìseal, longest river of the island, breaks its banks along its lower reach and carries away three bridges and a stretch of the coal line's embankment. The line is shut most of a year, and the ports live on stored coal.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-4554"><em>The Abhainn ìseal takes three bridges and the embankment</em>, 26 an Gearran, SE 34</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4555"></a>**28 an Giblean, SE 34** — *The coal line shuts and the ports live on stored coal* (Abhainn ìseal). With a mile of embankment gone under the Abhainn ìseal's flood the coal line shuts for want of ground to run on, and the ports that lived on what it carried, Cuan ruadh and Muileann chrom among them, turn to whatever coal they had laid by against a leaner week rather than a whole season.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0130"><em>The Abhainn ìseal floods</em>, 12 am Màrt, SE 34</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-4556"></a>**24 an t-Ògmhios, SE 34** — *Mary Coyle gives her first order as speaker* (Caol mhòr). Not yet a month in the chair, Mary Coyle calls the Moot together the evening word of the washed embankment reaches Caol mhòr and orders every port on the coal line's reach to open its own store and share it by the shire's count of hearths, the north sending south to Muileann chrom until the line can be mended.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0130"><em>The Abhainn ìseal floods</em>, 12 am Màrt, SE 34</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0131"></a>**26 an Cèitean, SE 35** — *The Hawk houses' own custodian* (Inis ìseal). The Hawk houses of Siorrachd Cnoc bheag name a custodian of their own, Raonaid nic Iain, and seat her at Inis ìseal. The high custodian at Seann Skell will not own her. The houses carry on as if he had.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5000"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, SE 35** — *The Hawk houses gather at Inis ìseal to name a custodian* (Inis ìseal). Witnesses of every Hawk house in Siorrachd Cnoc bheag crowd the hall at Inis ìseal and name Raonaid nic Iain custodian by a standing vote, each house setting meal, wool or honey on the altar's step before the hall breaks.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0131"><em>The Hawk houses' own custodian</em>, 26 an Cèitean, SE 35</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5001"></a>**11 an t-Iuchar, SE 35** — *Murchadh Ruadh gives Raonaid the kept feather* (Inis ìseal). Murchadh Ruadh of Baile fhraoich sets a white feather kept three generations in his own house into Raonaid nic Iain's hand at her naming, and she wears it pinned at her collar from that day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0131"><em>The Hawk houses' own custodian</em>, 26 an Cèitean, SE 35</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5002"></a>**12 an t-Iuchar, SE 35** — *The Hawk houses speak of a hawk for the shire's arms* (Cnoc bheag). Witnesses leaving Raonaid nic Iain's naming say openly that Siorrachd Cnoc bheag's white billet, the roll's mark for two ages, ought to be struck for a hawk, though no house yet carries the saying south.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5003"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, SE 35** — *Seann Skell's letter refusing Raonaid reaches Inis ìseal* (Inis ìseal). A three-line letter from the high custodian's house at Seann Skell in the south reaches Inis ìseal, naming no fault in Raonaid nic Iain but saying the Rite's own order of worship knows no office of a Hawk custodian and so cannot own her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0131"><em>The Hawk houses' own custodian</em>, 26 an Cèitean, SE 35</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5004"></a>**14 an t-Iuchar, SE 35** — *The Hawk houses carry on as if the custodian had been owned* (Inis ìseal). The Hawk houses fold the southern letter away unanswered and keep bringing their vigils and disputes to Raonaid nic Iain exactly as before, burying and marrying their own under no rite but hers.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0131"><em>The Hawk houses' own custodian</em>, 26 an Cèitean, SE 35</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0132"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, SE 35** — *Raonaid nic Iain at Inis ìseal* (Inis ìseal). Raonaid nic Iain, custodian of the Hawk houses, writes out the Hawk's order of worship, which until now was spoken and never written. The Hawk houses read it aloud once a year and keep the written copy locked away.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5005"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, SE 35** — *Raonaid begins setting the Hawk's order into a farm account-book* (Inis ìseal). Raonaid nic Iain starts writing the Hawk's spoken order of worship, till then carried only in a custodian's memory, into a farmer's account-book, sounding each line against the altar to match her own mother's mother's telling of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0132"><em>Raonaid nic Iain at Inis ìseal</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, SE 35</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5006"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, SE 35** — *The order finished and locked in the altar's oil-box* (Inis ìseal). Raonaid nic Iain finishes the written order at the turn of the year, reads it aloud once to the gathered houses, ties it with a strip of white feather and locks it into the iron box that once held the altar's lamp-oil.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0132"><em>Raonaid nic Iain at Inis ìseal</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, SE 35</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0132a"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, SE 35** — *A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag* (Cnoc bheag). The Hawk houses of Siorrachd Cnoc bheag ask the council to set a hawk on the shire's arms in place of the white billet the roll gave it. The council grants it, and the maor's seal is recut with a white hawk among its twelve crescents. It is the first change made to the roll at the asking of an order.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-5002"><em>The Hawk houses speak of a hawk for the shire's arms</em>, 12 an t-Iuchar, SE 35</a>.</span>

## The Years SE 36 – 40

- <a id="ev-EVI-5007"></a>**6 am Màrt, SE 36** — *A delegation from Inis ìseal asks the council for a hawk on the shire's seal* (Cathair mhòr). Five witnesses from the Hawk houses, Raonaid nic Iain among them, ride to Cathair dhearg to ask the council that Siorrachd Cnoc bheag's white billet be struck and a hawk set on the shire's arms in its place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0132a"><em>A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, SE 35</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5008"></a>**27 am Màrt, SE 36** — *The maor breaks the old die and presses the new seal* (Cnoc bheag). The maor of Siorrachd Cnoc bheag breaks the shire's old die before its assembled clerks and presses the recut seal, a white hawk among twelve crescents, into wax for the first time.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0132a"><em>A hawk for Siorrachd Cnoc bheag</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, SE 35</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0133"></a>**27 an Giblean, SE 36** — *Six dead at the Còmhrag* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). Six fighters die at the Còmhrag, the most in any year yet. The custodians of the Rite petition for its ending. The fair-wardens of Ceann leathan, whose town lives off the crowds, refuse.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5009"></a>**2 an Cèitean, SE 36** — *Six die at that year's Còmhrag* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). Six fighters, the most in any year yet, die on the trampled ground at Ceann leathan before that year's Còmhrag is called, one of them a boy of Baile ghlas not yet twenty.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0133"><em>Six dead at the Còmhrag</em>, 27 an Giblean, SE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5010"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, SE 36** — *The custodians' petition against the Còmhrag is refused* (Ceann leathan). The custodians of the southern Rite petition the fair-wardens of Ceann leathan in writing to end the Còmhrag after six deaths; the wardens read it and refuse within the hour, on the ground the town lives off the melee's crowds.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0133"><em>Six dead at the Còmhrag</em>, 27 an Giblean, SE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0134"></a>**6 an Dàmhair, SE 36** — *The circus at Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). In the year of the six dead An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn pitches at Ceann leathan and plays to the crowds who stay on after the melee. It is said the fair-wardens paid it to come.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5011"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, SE 36** — *The circus pitches at Ceann leathan after the six burials* (Ceann leathan). An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn pitches its tents on the melee's own trampled ground within a week of the six burials, and it is said, though never proved, that the fair-wardens paid it to come.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0134"><em>The circus at Ceann leathan</em>, 6 an Dàmhair, SE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0135"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, SE 36** — *The coal line reaches Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). The railway is carried through to the port of Ceann leathan, so that coal may be shipped from a second harbour. The quays of Ceann leathan are rebuilt for coal-ships, and the town outgrows its walls.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5012"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, SE 36** — *The first coal-ship loads by lamplight at Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). The first coal-ship out of Ceann leathan's rebuilt quays loads by lamplight on a winter tide, the harbour clerk noting only the hour, the tonnage and the shore gang's complaint of the cold.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0135"><em>The coal line reaches Ceann leathan</em>, 4 an t-Samhain, SE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0136"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, SE 36** — *Ros bheag's shipyard* (Ros bheag). Ros bheag on the west coast opens a yard for coal-ships, and the western ports need no longer send to Ros dhomhain for hulls. The shipwrights of Ros dhomhain protest to the guild court and lose.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5013"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, SE 36** — *Ros dhomhain's masters lose their protest at the guild court* (Cathair mhòr). The eldest masters of Ros dhomhain carry their protest against Ros bheag's new coal-ship yard to the guild court at Cathair dhearg and lose it in a single sitting, the court ruling a guild's charter binds no yard to a monopoly of the coast.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0136"><em>Ros bheag's shipyard</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, SE 36</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5014"></a>**1 am Faoilleach, SE 37** — *Iain Mapa proves the deep gallery* (Muileann chiar). Sent to measure a new shaft cut on a guild captain's thirty-year hunch, Iain mac Ruairidh finds the silver at Muileann chiar running richer with depth rather than thinner, the ore darker and heavier the further the gallery goes. He checks the figures three times before he writes them fair.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0137"><em>The silver at depth</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, SE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0137"></a>**1 am Faoilleach, SE 37** — *The silver at depth* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The silver seam at Muileann chiar, which the Dia-thìrich kept in their own hands through the humans' time, is found richer at depth than any had looked for. The town's old silver guild takes a charter under the restored custom. Iain Mapa, working there since the Board sent him, measures the new faces.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-5014"><em>Iain Mapa proves the deep gallery</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, SE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0137a"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, SE 37** — *The eastern blank-houses* (Baile dhìreach). More silver comes up from Muileann chiar than the mint at Cathair dhearg can refine. The Crown gives the villages of the eastern hills the refining of the guild's bar, with the gold washed from the stream below Baile dhìreach, into blanks for the realm-coin. The mint strikes them. The villages are paid by weight.
- <a id="ev-V-0138"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, SE 37** — *Dùn thais in the west* (Dùn thais). Dùn thais on the west coast is granted a court of the sea of its own, to judge salvage and wreck along its shore. At its first sitting it awards a raider's hulk to the fishermen who drove it aground.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5015"></a>**6 an Dàmhair, SE 37** — *The guild masters read the survey entire* (Muileann chiar). Iain carries the deep gallery's figures to the guild hall himself and unrolls them before three masters who argue over the timbering a new shaft will need. He tells them plainly it will hold only if timbered as he has drawn it, and not an inch cheaper.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0137"><em>The silver at depth</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, SE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5016"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, SE 37** — *The silver guild of Muileann chiar chartered anew* (Muileann chiar). On the strength of the deep gallery's yield the council renews under the restored custom the charter the humans' own Administration had let stand and then let lapse, binding the guild's captains to the Crown's tithe on every bar struck and giving the guild the courts' weight behind its bindings.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0137"><em>The silver at depth</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, SE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5017"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, SE 37** — *Gold found in the stream below Baile dhìreach* (Baile dhìreach). A village smith washing his pan of an evening finds fine gold in the gravel of the stream that turns his forge's own wheel, and tells a maor's clerk the plain truth when the coin he has put by draws the clerk's question rather than invent a lie he would have to keep.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0137a"><em>The eastern blank-houses</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, SE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5018"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, SE 37** — *The first blanks struck for the mint* (Baile dhìreach). More silver comes up from Muileann chiar than the mint at Cathair dhearg can refine, and the council gives the eastern hill villages the refining of the guild's bar, with the gold washed below Baile dhìreach, into blanks for the realm-coin, paid by weight; the first blanks go north in am Faoilleach.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0137a"><em>The eastern blank-houses</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, SE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0139"></a>**2 an Gearran, SE 38** — *Dùn thais in the east* (Dùn thais). The other Dùn thais, in the east, seat of its own shire, builds a covered market for the hill farms. For ten years the royal record confuses the courts of the two towns, until Tormod Pinn marks them west and east.
- <a id="ev-V-0139a"></a>**18 an Dàmhair, SE 38** — *Siorrachd Doire chaol* (Doire chaol). Doire chaol, the village laid out south of the capital for the families of the royal household, has grown too great for the maor of Baile chiar to govern from his seat. The council cuts it out as a shire of its own, the only shire made since the drawing.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5019"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, SE 38** — *Iain Mapa marries Mòr nic Dhòmhnaill* (Muileann chiar). Iain marries Mòr, a refiner's daughter of Muileann chiar who first proved his own scale a hair off true in front of three of the guild's captains. They are married at the guild hall in am Faoilleach, her father giving her hand and the guild's captains standing witness in place of Iain's own western kin.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0137"><em>The silver at depth</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, SE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5020"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, SE 38** — *Dùn thais in the west granted a sea court* (Dùn thais). The western Dùn thais is granted a court of the sea to judge salvage and wreck along its shore, after a wrecked hulk driven ashore proves too rich a prize for custom alone to divide. The court's first sitting, held on the strand, awards the wreck whole to the crews who drove it aground.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0138"><em>Dùn thais in the west</em>, 3 an Dàmhair, SE 37</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5021"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, SE 38** — *Dùn thais in the east opens its covered market* (Dùn thais). The eastern Dùn thais raises a covered market at its own shire's charge for the hill farms that had traded in its square uncovered since the town was walled, its first trading held under a roof that smells more of new-cut wood than of the produce it shelters.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0139"><em>Dùn thais in the east</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 38</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5022"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, SE 38** — *The royal record confuses the two Dùn thais* (Dùn thais). A clerk at Cathair dhearg files the western court's petition and the eastern market's petition against the one town's name, both signed only "Dùn thais", and a second clerk's hand-correction holds only until the next season's post brings the same confusion again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0139"><em>Dùn thais in the east</em>, 2 an Gearran, SE 38</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5023"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, SE 38** — *Baile chiar's maor petitions to cut out Doire chaol* (Baile chiar). The maor of Baile chiar writes plainly that Doire chaol, grown from a scattering of household-clerks' houses into a town proper, has outgrown a seat five miles distant, and asks that it be given a maor of its own rather than go on being governed badly at second hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0139a"><em>Siorrachd Doire chaol</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, SE 38</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5024"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 38** — *Siorrachd Doire chaol cut from Baile chiar* (Doire chaol). The council grants the petition before the summer is old, the only shire cut new from an older one since the original drawing, Doire chaol entered onto the roll with its own arms, its own dues, and a maor of its own choosing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0139a"><em>Siorrachd Doire chaol</em>, 18 an Dàmhair, SE 38</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0140"></a>**23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 39** — *The dead and not dead of Doire uaine* (Marbh-bheò Doire uaine). Herders near Doire uaine will not graze the hills above the town, where old writings tell of a thing that is dead and does not rest. A shepherd is lost there. The magistrate enters wolves.
- <a id="ev-V-0141"></a>**1 an t-Iuchar, SE 39** — *The fall at Muileann dhearg* (Muileann dhearg). A gallery of the reopened Cill ghlas district gives way under Muileann dhearg, along a line the surveyors had marked as sound. Thirty-one hewers die. It is small beside the Rending. It is the same fault.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5025"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, SE 39** — *Iain Mapa rides through the night to Muileann dhearg* (Muileann dhearg). Word of the fall reaches Muileann chiar by a rider sent without urgency, and Iain Mapa, two seasons into the silver works and no longer reckoned a mine matter by the Board, rides the thirty miles through the night rather than wait for morning, and goes down on the second rope with a lamp and a level.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0141"><em>The fall at Muileann dhearg</em>, 1 an t-Iuchar, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5026"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, SE 39** — *Iain Mapa lays his own old maps against the new fault* (Muileann dhearg). With maps sent up from the silver guild's own store, older and truer than anything the Board keeps at Cathair mhòr, Iain Mapa finds the broken ground under the fallen gallery runs exactly where the Rending's own line ran three ages before, marked by an older hand with a single word: left, let be.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0141"><em>The fall at Muileann dhearg</em>, 1 an t-Iuchar, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5027"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, SE 39** — *The thirty-one are buried in a single ground* (Muileann dhearg). The dead of the fall are buried at the edge of Muileann dhearg's own burying-yard, thirty-one graves broken in two days by every man in the town not needed underground, the district's custodian reading over each grave in turn at the families' own asking, and Iain Mapa standing the whole of it with his hat in his hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0141"><em>The fall at Muileann dhearg</em>, 1 an t-Iuchar, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5028"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, SE 39** — *Iain Mapa writes a letter naming the fault, and does not send it*. At his own table at Muileann chiar, Iain Mapa writes to the Board naming the fault at Cill ghlas by its true line and setting it beside the survey the Board filed and never circulated three years before; he reads it through twice, folds it, and puts it unsealed in the drawer that holds his old receipt.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0141"><em>The fall at Muileann dhearg</em>, 1 an t-Iuchar, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0142"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39** — *The rules of the shafts*. After this lesser echo of the old fall of Scàineadh Cill ghlas, new rules for digging are made. They are for Dia-thìrich workers. In the workings where Tuathaich labour they are kept loosely, and by intent.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-5026"><em>Iain Mapa lays his own old maps against the new fault</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0143"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39** — *The timber at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). At the pits about Àth leathan, where Dia-thìrich overseers work Tuathaich hands, the new rules of timbering are posted and not paid for. The overseers' books, which came later to the library, show the timber ordered and never delivered.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5029"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39** — *A shepherd lost above Doire uaine* (Doire uaine). A shepherd new to the country puts his flock to the one shoulder of hill the town's shepherds will not graze, where the old writings tell of the Marbh-bheò, and does not come down. His dog returns alone; the town finds only his crook, driven upright into the turf.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0140"><em>The dead and not dead of Doire uaine</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5030"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39** — *The magistrate enters wolves at Doire uaine* (Doire uaine). The magistrate writes wolves as the cause in the shire's own book, a finding no shepherd argues and none believes, since no wolf has been seen on that hill in living memory. He tells the shepherd's mother the book wanted a cause it could hold.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0140"><em>The dead and not dead of Doire uaine</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5031"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39** — *Iain Mapa keeps a second copy of the guild's charter* (Muileann chiar). Iain writes the silver guild's new charter into his own private book beside the receipt he carried from the Sloc Mòr and the deep gallery's own figures, telling Mòr at last that the Board never once told him his first survey of the thinning vein had proved true.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0137"><em>The silver at depth</em>, 1 am Faoilleach, SE 37</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0140"><em>The dead and not dead of Doire uaine</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5032"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39** — *Mary Coyle writes to the Board naming Àth leathan's undelivered timber* (Caol mhòr). Reading a copy of the Board's new digging rules brought north by a carter, Mary Coyle writes in the Moot's own hand asking that the rules be kept in fact at the western pits as well as in the posting, and names Àth leathan and the ordered timber that never left the yard at Ceann mhòr.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0143"><em>The timber at Àth leathan</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5033"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39** — *The Board answers the Moot in three lines and files the matter* (Àth leathan). The Board thanks the Moot for its concern and states that Àth leathan's timber has been referred to the district overseer for his report; no report is ever filed, and Mary Coyle's letter is kept, unanswered further, in the press at Cathair mhòr where papers go that the Board has no further use for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0143"><em>The timber at Àth leathan</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, SE 39</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5034"></a>**23 an t-Iuchar, SE 40** — *Ailean Leabhar is found dead at his own desk* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). On the third day of an t-Sultain, Mòrag nic Coinnich finds Ailean Leabhar at his desk at Muileann chaol, the harvest returns for Siorrachd Doire chaol open under his hand and his pen laid down beside them rather than dropped, so that he seems, she says after, to have finished the line he was writing before he stopped.
- <a id="ev-V-0144"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, SE 40** — *Mòrag nic Coinnich, keeper* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Ailean Leabhar dies at Muileann chaol, and Mòrag nic Coinnich becomes keeper of the library. She begins the custom, kept ever since, of writing beside each item whence it came.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-5034"><em>Ailean Leabhar is found dead at his own desk</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, SE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5035"></a>**8 an t-Sultain, SE 40** — *Ailean Leabhar is buried in the ground behind the Library* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Ailean Leabhar is buried two days after at Muileann chaol, in a small ground behind the Library itself where no keeper had been buried before him, the town turning out near to the last household, and Mòrag nic Coinnich reads over him only his own words, that the Library settles nothing and only keeps.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0144"><em>Mòrag nic Coinnich, keeper</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, SE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5036"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, SE 40** — *Mòrag nic Coinnich finds an unfinished note among Ailean Leabhar's papers* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Going through the old keeper's desk in her first month as keeper, Mòrag nic Coinnich finds one sheet in his own hand, undated beyond an old year, reading only that what the Library is not sent it cannot keep, and to ask the shires again; she cannot say whether it was a note to himself or the start of a letter, and keeps it unfiled in her own drawer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0144"><em>Mòrag nic Coinnich, keeper</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, SE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0145"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, SE 40** — *The pit families of Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). After the fall at Muileann dhearg forty hewers' families leave Achadh dhomhain for the fishing ports of the south. The Guild of Hewers binds sixty apprentices to fill its rolls. None of them are Tuathaich.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5037"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, SE 40** — *Sixty apprentices are bound at Achadh dhomhain, and not one is Tuathaich* (Achadh dhomhain). The Guild of Hewers binds sixty boys in its own hall at Achadh dhomhain to fill the rolls the fall thinned by thirty-one, each swearing with a hand laid on a lump of coal while his father stands behind him in a line the length of the hall, and the charter that reserves the oath to Dia-thìreach applicants is kept to the letter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0145"><em>The pit families of Achadh dhomhain</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, SE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5038"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, SE 40** — *A family with no dead in the fall leaves Achadh dhomhain regardless* (Achadh dhomhain). Among the forty households that quit Achadh dhomhain for the southern ports that autumn are families who buried no one in the fall, saying to whoever asks that a town may grieve its thirty-one and go on living beside their graves, but a household does not choose to raise its own sons under ground a survey has already misjudged once.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0145"><em>The pit families of Achadh dhomhain</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, SE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0146"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, SE 40** — *Fire at the fair* (Fèill Muileann òg). On the eve of Samhain fire runs through the stalls of the fair at Muileann òg. The next day the fair's court sits in a field, and the fair goes on. Oighrig nic Mhathain, toll-mistress since the first fair, dies of her burns.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5039"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, SE 40** — *Oighrig nic Mhathain is burned beating back the fire with her own cloak* (Fèill Muileann òg). Caught in the fairground when the fire runs on Samhain eve, Oighrig nic Mhathain beats at the burning canvas with her own cloak until the worst of it is turned from the stalls that hold a dozen towns' whole trade, and does not leave the ground until the last flame along the weavers' row has burned itself out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0146"><em>Fire at the fair</em>, 31 an Dàmhair, SE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0147"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, SE 40** — *The Tuathaich wool carts* (Muileann leathan). The Rail Board will not carry goods sent by the Moot, pleading the fair's rule on factors. The wool of the north goes south to Muileann òg by cart, five days on the road, and is sold by factors when it comes.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5040"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, SE 40** — *Mary Coyle asks the Board whether its reading of the factor rule is new* (Caol mhòr). When the Rail Board refuses to carry the north's wool on the strength of the fair's own rule on factors, Mary Coyle writes a second, shorter letter asking only whether the reading is new or has simply never before been turned against the north's own goods; the Board does not answer it, and a clerk files it beside the first.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0147"><em>The Tuathaich wool carts</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, SE 40</a>.</span>

## The Years SE 41 – 45

- <a id="ev-V-0148"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, SE 41** — *The Tuathaich carters' road* (Àth fhada). The carters of the northern wool go to the fair by Cnoc ghorm, Àth fhada and the old road down to Inis àrsaidh, and the Tuathaich villages on the way open inns for them. In the north the road is called the Carters' Road. In the south it has no name.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5500"></a>**26 an Gearran, SE 41** — *Daniel Frayne rides the wool carts south* (Muileann leathan). With the Rail Board still refusing the Moot's goods, the north's wool goes south by cart, and Daniel Frayne asks leave to ride with the second train, five days on the old way by Cnoc ghorm, Àth fhada and Inis àrsaidh to the fair at Muileann òg.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0147"><em>The Tuathaich wool carts</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, SE 40</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0148"><em>The Tuathaich carters' road</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, SE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0149"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, SE 41** — *Dubhan's childhood*. Dubhan grows up watching a caste that does not age hold every true advantage on an island where his own forebears were pushed to the edge. The coal was never his to inherit.
- <a id="ev-V-0150"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41** — *The Moot's pit register* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr begins a register of Tuathaich hewers killed or maimed in the western pits, for no Dia-thìreach book counts them. Mary Coyle's clerks enter the first year's names on the families' own word. The register is kept to this day and has never been sent south.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5501"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41** — *The first lamp lit at Àth fhada* (Àth fhada). A widow of Àth fhada who has fed carters at her own table for two winters begins taking payment for it, keeping a lamp lit past every other house's hour. Two more households on the road do the same within the season, and carters find their beds by the lights alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0148"><em>The Tuathaich carters' road</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, SE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5502"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41** — *The north's name and the south's silence* (Àth fhada). Frayne asks the widow at Àth fhada what the carters call their road and learns it has long been called the Carters' Road in the north, its name simply grown to fit the wool's going by cart. He learns too that no map south of Cnoc ghorm troubles to name the road at all, and writes both facts down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0148"><em>The Tuathaich carters' road</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, SE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5503"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41** — *A season's wages weighed against the road* (Inis àrsaidh). Waiting out a flood at a crossing short of Inis àrsaidh, Frayne hears from a shunting family how the road's five days are reckoned against a season's whole earning, a toll no southern ledger is ever asked to set against the fair's own profit. He writes the figure down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0148"><em>The Tuathaich carters' road</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, SE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5504"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41** — *Mary Coyle opens the register of the hurt* (Caol mhòr). Mary Coyle tells the Moot's clerks that the Board keeps no true count of the Tuathaich dead and maimed of the western pits, and that the Moot will begin a book naming them on the families' own word, since no other word will be offered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0150"><em>The Moot's pit register</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5505"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41** — *The first name entered in Clàr nan Leòn* (Caol mhòr). The widow of Àth fhada's husband, lost under the western pits, is the first name Daniel Frayne writes into the new register, carried south by a neighbour rather than wait on the widow's own journey. Frayne sets the pen down before the ink is dry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0150"><em>The Moot's pit register</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5506"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41** — *The keel laid at Ros mhòr* (Ros mhòr). Shipwrights turned out of the southern guild yards gather enough coin and timber at last to lay a keel of their own at Ros mhòr. Harry Marlow, grey now, cuts it to the humans' old lines, low and full in the bow, that the southern guilds no longer let a Tuathaich hand build.
- <a id="ev-V-0151"></a>**5 an Cèitean, SE 42** — *Ros mhòr's boatyard* (Ros mhòr). Tuathaich boatbuilders turned out of the guild yards open a boatyard at Ros mhòr in the north. Its boats are built to the humans' old lines and are swifter than anything in the south.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVI-5506"><em>The keel laid at Ros mhòr</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0152"></a>**31 an t-Iuchar, SE 42** — *Tormod Pinn* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill lays down the office of royal chronicler. Tormod mac Sheumais follows her, called Tormod Pinn for the speed of his hand. He keeps the record for more than twenty years and writes more of it than any before or since.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5507"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, SE 42** — *A second copy of the register kept apart* (Muileann leathan). By the year's end the register holds above thirty names. A second copy is made against fire or flood and kept at a house in Muileann leathan, so that no single hand's slipping can lose the names a second time.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0150"><em>The Moot's pit register</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, SE 41</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5508"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, SE 42** — *Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's last entry* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Feeling her hand begin to shake on a long day's writing, Gormshuil lays down the office of royal chronicler after four and twenty years, her final entry a plain list of what the chronicle under her hand had never held: the northern towns' own accounts, the humans' old treaties, and the Board's surveys left unrolled.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0152"><em>Tormod Pinn</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, SE 42</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5509"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, SE 42** — *Tormod Pinn copies the list of gaps* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Tormod mac Sheumais, called Tormod Pinn for the speed of his hand, succeeds Gormshuil as royal chronicler and opens his own first book by copying her last list whole, striking nothing from it, so it is not lost to be rewritten by a less patient hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0152"><em>Tormod Pinn</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, SE 42</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVI-5510"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, SE 42** — *The first Ros mhòr hull launched* (Ros mhòr). Built on evenings and Sabbaths through a year, the yard's first hull takes the water clean at Ros mhòr, swifter than anything the southern yards have launched in a long season. Harry Marlow tells the men beside him he means to live to see the north sail hulls built with no southern guild's leave.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0151"><em>Ros mhòr's boatyard</em>, 5 an Cèitean, SE 42</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0153"></a>**25 an Giblean, SE 43** — *Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's last entry* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Tormod Pinn copies into the front of his first book the last entry Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill made as chronicler, a list of what the record lacks: the northern towns' own accounts, the humans' treaties in their own tongue, and the Board's surveys. He adds nothing to it.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5511"></a>**2 an Cèitean, SE 43** — *Tormod Pinn adds his own line to the list of gaps* (Muileann chaol). Riding the southern circuit his predecessor once rode, Tormod Pinn adds beneath Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's list of what the chronicle lacks a line of his own, that a gap named is worth more than a gap forgotten, and copies both into the chest that goes to the Library.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0153"><em>Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's last entry</em>, 25 an Giblean, SE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0154"></a>**3 an Cèitean, SE 43** — *Dry years at Achadh shean* (Tiormachd Achadh shean). Dry years come again to the country about Achadh shean, where the Long Drought settled in the humans' time. This time the council sends grain up the coal line and pays for it out of the Sloc Mòr's share. No one in the shire dies of hunger, and the chronicler records it.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5512"></a>**12 an t-Iuchar, SE 43** — *The maor of Achadh shean petitions early* (Achadh shean). With three wells of the drove road gone brackish and a fourth dry to the stone, the maor of Siorrachd Achadh shean writes south before the second month of the dry is out rather than wait for the harvest itself to fail, and asks that a man argues with a poor harvest but a well gone to stone argues with no one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0154"><em>Dry years at Achadh shean</em>, 3 an Cèitean, SE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0155"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, SE 43** — *The wells of Siorrachd Achadh shean* (Achadh shean). The maor of Siorrachd Achadh shean has twelve wells dug to the rock along the drove road, each marked with the name of the shire and of the council. Water is drawn from four of them still.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5513"></a>**7 am Faoilleach, SE 44** — *A fifth well dug dry on a dowser's word* (Achadh shean). Of the twelve wells the maor of Achadh shean has cut along the drove road, one stands dry from the day it is dug, sited on a dowser's hazel rather than any surveyor's word, and the well-diggers own the fact afterward without much shame in the owning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-V-0155"><em>The wells of Siorrachd Achadh shean</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, SE 43</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-V-0156"></a>**9 am Faoilleach, SE 44** — *Grain by the coal line* (Achadh shean). The grain for Achadh shean comes from the store at Cathair fhada, and for the first time it goes by the coal line. The Rail Board charges the council for the carriage.
- <a id="ev-EVI-5514"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, SE 44** — *The first wagons reach Achadh shean in the rain* (Achadh shean).
